Amp.Amp Model: Selects the amp type; each type loads its own starting values for tone, master, negative feedback, tonestack and speaker curve.
Amp.Gain: Preamp gain: higher moves from clean through breakup to full distortion; on amps with no master it acts as volume, and lower can brighten via treble peaker.
Amp.Bass: Passive tonestack bass: higher adds low end, lower tightens; interacts with Mid and Treble like the original amp's knob.
Amp.Mid: Passive tonestack mids: higher adds body and push, lower scoops the midrange; interacts with Bass and Treble like the original amp.
Amp.Treble: Passive tonestack treble: higher brightens and adds bite, lower darkens; interacts with Bass and Mid like the original amp.
Amp.Master: Master volume: higher drives the virtual power amp for more bloom, compression and power-amp distortion; too high muddies high-gain clean-PA amps.
Amp.Presence: Power-amp high-end via negative feedback: higher adds treble sparkle and edge, lower softens; becomes a simple shelf with power amp modelling off.
Amp.Depth: Power-amp low-end boost via negative feedback (0..10): higher adds bass weight and thump, lower tightens the bottom.
Amp.Level: Output level of the Amp block in dB; changes loudness only, not the tone or distortion.
Amp.Low Cut: High-pass filter at the amp input: raise the frequency to tighten the amp and cut low-end flub before distortion.
Amp.High Cut: Low-pass filter at the end of the preamp: lower for a darker, smoother tone; higher for brighter.
Amp.Output EQ Type: Graphic EQ style for the Amp's built-in output EQ (band count and Q); the Mark type is a 5-band 80/240/750/2200/6600 Hz EQ.
Amp.Output EQ Location: Where the output graphic EQ sits: Output (after the power amp, EQs the distortion) or PrePowerAmp (between preamp and power amp, as on Mark amps).
Amp.Output EQ Enabled: Turns the Amp block's built-in graphic EQ on or off.
Amp.Output EQ 80 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 80 Hz, -12..12 dB: boost for low-end thump, cut to tighten; cut here plus mid scoop gives the Mark V-curve.
Amp.Output EQ 240 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 240 Hz, -12..12 dB: boost for warmth and body, cut to reduce muddiness.
Amp.Output EQ 750 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 750 Hz, -12..12 dB: boost for midrange push and cut-through, cut for a scooped sound.
Amp.Output EQ 2200 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 2200 Hz, -12..12 dB: boost for presence and pick attack, cut to reduce harshness.
Amp.Output EQ 6600 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 6600 Hz, -12..12 dB: boost for air and sizzle, cut to tame fizz.
Amp.Balance: Left/right balance of the block output, -100..100; 0 is centred.
Amp.Bypass Mode: What the block passes when bypassed: THRU passes the dry signal, MUTE silences it.
Amp.Scene Ignore: When ON, scene changes leave this block's bypass and channel state alone.
Amp.Tonestack Freq: Centre frequency of the tone controls (200..2000 Hz): moves where Bass/Mid/Treble act; defaults per amp type.
Amp.Bright Cap: Value of the bright (treble peaker) capacitor that the Bright switch uses: higher makes the preamp brighter, lower duller.
Amp.Wslpf: Undocumented: likely a low-pass filter (400..40000 Hz) around a preamp waveshaper (clipper) stage.
Amp.XFormer Low Freq: Low-frequency bandwidth limit of the output transformer (5..500 Hz): higher thins the bass, lower extends it.
Amp.XFormer Hi Freq: High-frequency bandwidth limit of the output transformer (4..40 kHz): lower darkens the top end, higher extends it.
Amp.Tonestack Location: Where the tonestack sits: PRE (preamp input), MID (between last two triodes), POST (before power amp), END (after power amp); PRE-MID undocumented.
Amp.Input Select: How a stereo input feeds the mono amp: LEFT, RIGHT, or SUM L+R (default).
Amp.Offset1: Undocumented: likely a DC bias offset (-1..1) for the first preamp clipping stage.
Amp.Cliptype2: Undocumented: likely the clipping curve used by an internal preamp stage (soft, hard, triode etc.).
Amp.Supply Sag: Power-supply impedance: higher gives more voltage droop and a compressed, spongy feel, mostly when the Master pushes the power amp.
Amp.Negative Feedback: Power-amp negative feedback: higher is tighter and brighter but can be harsh at high Master; lower is looser and grittier.
Amp.Presence Frequency: Multiplier (0.1..10) on the Presence control's centre frequency: higher moves Presence to higher treble.
Amp.Low Freq: Speaker LF resonance frequency (40..400 Hz) of the virtual impedance curve: where the power amp's low-end bump sits.
Amp.LF Reso: Amount of speaker low-frequency resonance: higher adds a stronger power-amp bass bump at Low Freq.
Amp.Depth Frequency: Centre frequency of the Depth control (50..500 Hz): moves where the Depth bass boost acts.
Amp.Drivetype: Drive circuit topology (e.g. jumped channels, tweed); set by the amp type so Gain behaves like the original circuit.
Amp.Master Vol Cap: Value of the bright cap across the Master Volume: higher adds treble as the Master is turned down.
Amp.Wshpf: Undocumented: likely a high-pass filter (2..2000 Hz) around a preamp waveshaper (clipper) stage.
Amp.Harmonics: Cathode follower harmonics: higher increases interaction between virtual tubes for softer distortion.
Amp.Tonestack Type: Substitutes another amp's passive tonestack (or ACTIVE: +/-12 dB non-interacting controls) to make hybrids; DEFAULT keeps the model's own.
Amp.B+ Time Constant: Power-supply speed (1..100 ms): lower sags fast, accenting pick attack then compressing; extremes cause ripple or ghost notes.
Amp.Grid Bias: Power tube grid bias (0..100%): lower approaches Class-B with more crossover grit, higher approaches Class-A.
Amp.Fbtype: Undocumented: likely selects which amp's negative-feedback network voicing the power amp uses.
Amp.Pi Ratio: Undocumented: likely the phase inverter gain or balance ratio (0..1) in the power amp.
Amp.Bright: Bright switch (treble peaker): ON adds treble, most noticeable at lower Gain; amount set by Bright Cap.
Amp.Boost: Built-in input boost: ON drives the amp harder like a pedal with drive at 0 and level up, set by Boost Type and Boost Level.
Amp.LF Q: Sharpness of the speaker LF resonance: higher gives a narrower, peakier low-end bump, lower a broader one.
Amp.Preamp Bias: Bias of the last triode (-1..1): near 0 gives mostly odd harmonics (open, aggressive); away from 0 adds even harmonics (warmer, can muddy).
Amp.High Freq: Speaker HF resonance frequency (400..4000 Hz) from voice-coil inductance: where the power amp's treble bump sits.
Amp.HF Reso: Amount of speaker high-frequency resonance: higher adds a stronger power-amp treble bump at High Freq.
Amp.Cut: Cut switch: ON reduces low frequencies into the amp to tighten the tone and reduce low-end flub.
Amp.XFormer Drive: Output transformer core saturation: higher simulates a smaller transformer that saturates more easily, adding low-end distortion.
Amp.Input Trim: Extra gain into the model (0.1..10) without changing frequency response: higher adds gain and distortion, lower cleans up.
Amp.Tube Hardness: How sharply the tubes enter saturation: lower gives softer, rounder distortion; higher harder clipping with more sparkle.
Amp.Master Vol Location: Where the Master sits: PRE-PI (most amps), POST-PI (Class-A types) or PRE-TRIODE (Hipower types); changes how the power amp distorts.
Amp.Speaker Drive: Speaker cone distortion and gentle compression from pushing the speaker; interacts with Master, good for old edge-of-breakup tones.
Amp.XFormer Matching: Output transformer turns ratio: lower clips the power tubes later (more PI/grid clipping); higher clips sooner with stronger speaker resonance.
Amp.Screen Frequency: Resonant frequency of the virtual power tube screen filter.
Amp.Screen Q: Q (sharpness) of the virtual power tube screen filter.
Amp.Saturation Switch: Saturation mod between preamp and tonestack for thicker, more aggressive distortion; ON (IDEAL) is the same with hotter output.
Amp.EQ 2K Hz: Built-in output graphic EQ band at 2 kHz, -12..12 dB (multi-band EQ types): boost for presence and pick bite, cut to reduce harshness.
Amp.EQ 4K Hz: Built-in output graphic EQ band at 4 kHz, -12..12 dB (multi-band EQ types): boost for edge and clarity, cut to tame harsh upper mids.
Amp.EQ 8K Hz: Built-in output graphic EQ band at 8 kHz, -12..12 dB (multi-band EQ types): boost for air and sizzle, cut to tame fizz.
Amp.Bias Excursion: How far the power tube grid bias shifts when overdriven (0..200%): higher gives more sag, compression and blocking-style distortion.
Amp.Excursion Time: How fast the power tube coupling cap charges while grids conduct (0.25..25 ms), shaping the onset of bias excursion.
Amp.Recovery Time: How fast the power tube coupling cap bleeds off after grid conduction (0.5..50 ms): longer gives slower recovery from bias shift.
Amp.Triode 2 Plate Freq: Cutoff of the plate cap on the last preamp triode: lower smooths highs and reduces fizz and noise, higher is brighter.
Amp.Triode 1 Plate Freq: Cutoff of the plate cap on the second-to-last preamp triode: lower smooths highs and reduces fizz and noise, higher is brighter.
Amp.Power Tube Type: Virtual power tube type (EL34, 6L6, EL84, KT88 etc.): sets knee voltage and plate characteristics that colour power-amp distortion.
Amp.Preamp Tube Type: Virtual preamp tube type (12AX7 variants, ECC83, 7025, EF86): changes preamp tube characteristics and distortion feel.
Amp.Out Comp Clarity: Bass response of the output compressor: higher lets more low end through for clarity under compression.
Amp.Q: Input EQ filter width: higher is narrower and more surgical, lower broader.
Amp.Frequency: Input EQ filter frequency (100..10000 Hz), applied before the preamp so it changes how the amp distorts.
Amp.Gain 2: Input EQ filter gain (-20..20 dB): boosting before the preamp adds drive at that frequency, cutting removes it.
Amp.Overdrive: Second overdrive gain stage on certain models (e.g. Mark lead drive, 'Ratio' or 'Lead Master'): higher adds lead gain and saturation.
Amp.Out Compression: Output compressor amount: higher reduces the amp's output dynamic range for a more even, compressed sound.
Amp.Out Comp Threshold: Output compressor threshold (-60..0 dB): lower starts compressing quieter signals.
Amp.Master Vol Trim: Range scaling of the Master (0.1..10): above 1.0 adds power-amp gain and distortion, below reduces it.
Amp.Fat: Fat switch: ON shifts the tonestack centre frequency to emphasise mids and add body.
Amp.Definition: Tilt EQ at the amp input: positive adds highs and cuts lows for clarity, negative adds lows and cuts highs, before distortion.
Amp.Compression: Cathode follower compression (0..100%): higher compresses and smooths the preamp more.
Amp.Grid Clipping: Cathode follower grid clipping: lower is the soft response of classic tubes, higher the abrupt clipping of modern tubes.
Amp.Version: Undocumented: internal model version marker with a fixed value of 0; leave unchanged.
Amp.High Cut 2: Hi Cut Freq at the end of the preamp (200..20000 Hz): lower for a darker, smoother tone, higher for brighter.
Amp.Power Type: Virtual power supply: AC models rectifier ripple (can cause ghost notes with low sag), DC is ripple-free.
Amp.AC Line Frequency: Mains frequency of the AC virtual supply (50 or 60 Hz typical), setting the ripple frequency.
Amp.Hardness: Power Tube Hardness: adjusts the power tubes' knee voltage; higher gives more abrupt power-amp clipping, lower softer clipping.
Amp.Frequency 2: Bias tremolo rate (0.2..20 Hz): how fast the power tube bias is modulated.
Amp.Depth 2: Bias tremolo depth (0..100%): higher gives stronger, self-ducking tremolo; extremes can add crossover distortion.
Amp.Ratio: Undocumented: likely the power tube bias arrangement: FIXED bias, or cathode bias with a SHARED or SPLIT cathode resistor.
Amp.Cathode Resistance: Power tube cathode resistor for cathode-biased amps: higher biases colder toward Class-B with more crossover distortion.
Amp.Cathode Time Const: Time constant of the power tube cathode RC network (1..100 ms) on cathode-biased amps, setting how fast the bias shifts.
Amp.Dynimp: Dynamic Damping: adjusts the modelled plate impedance (plate characteristics) of the virtual power tubes; direction not documented.
Amp.Preamp Sag: ON behaves like an integrated head or combo whose preamp sags with the supply; OFF simulates a separate preamp and power amp.
Amp.High Treble: Extra treble control: higher adds zing, lower tames harsh highs.
Amp.Mismatch: Undocumented: likely the imbalance between the push-pull power tubes (-1..1), adding even harmonics.
Amp.Input Dynamics: Input dynamics processor (-10..10): below 0 compresses for a smoother feel, above 0 expands for punchier, crunchier response.
Amp.HF Slope: Voice-coil inductance slope (typical 3.0..4.5): lower gives more midrange, higher a more scooped, sizzly sound.
Amp.Variac: Relative AC line voltage (50..150%): changes the amp's feel and headroom, with volume compensated.
Amp.Type: Input EQ filter type: LOWSHELF, PEAKING, HIGHSHELF or TILT EQ, applied before the preamp.
Amp.Gridhardness: Undocumented: likely how abruptly the power tube grids clip when driven into conduction (10..100%).
Amp.Pres. Shift: Presence Shift: ON models the pull-shift 'Lead Presence' found on some amps (e.g. certain USA types).
Amp.Saturation Drive: Amount of the Saturation mod's drive (1..10): higher adds thicker, more aggressive distortion when Saturation is on.
Amp.Preamp Bias Excursion: How far the preamp bias shifts when the virtual triodes are overdriven: higher adds more sag and compression to distortion.
Amp.Triode2extime: Undocumented: likely the bias excursion time of preamp triode 2 (0.1..100 ms).
Amp.Triode2rectime: Undocumented: likely the bias recovery time of preamp triode 2 (0.2..200 ms).
Amp.Out Comp Type: Output compressor type: OUTPUT compresses the output; FEEDBACK also varies drive with picking; GAIN ENHANCER mimics a loud amp's reinforcement.
Amp.Type 2: Undocumented: likely the type of a preamp compression stage, AUTHENTIC (as the original circuit) or IDEAL.
Amp.Triode1ratio: Undocumented: likely the gain ratio of preamp triode 1 (-200..200%).
Amp.Hardness 2: Undocumented: likely the hardness (how sharply it clips) of the cathode follower stage, alongside its Compression and Grid Clipping.
Amp.PI Bias Excursion: How far the phase inverter bias shifts when overdriven (0..200%): higher adds more power-amp sag and compression.
Speaker power compression ('chunka chunka'): higher adds more compression and thump; set 0 with a real tube amp and cab.
Amp.Speaker Time Const: Voice-coil thermal time constant (100..10000 ms): lower makes speaker compression attack and release faster.
Amp.Boost Level: Level of the built-in input boost (0..24 dB): higher drives the amp harder for more gain.
Amp.Boost Type: Colour of the built-in input boost, based on real pedals (T808, SUPER OD, TREBLE BOOST etc.), each with its own EQ.
Amp.Output Mode: FRFR for flat monitors or recording; SS PWR AMP + CAB relies on a real guitar cab for speaker compression.
Amp.Speaker Compliance: Nonlinear behaviour of the virtual speaker (default 50%, typical for guitar speakers).
Amp.Speaker Impedance: Relative nominal speaker impedance: 0.5 simulates a 4-ohm speaker on an 8-ohm tap, 2.0 a 16-ohm speaker.
Amp.Speaker Imp. Curve: Speaker impedance curve modelling amp/speaker interaction, a large share of the cab feel; usually matched to the cab used.
Amp.Cab Resonance: How strongly the speaker impedance curve's cabinet resonance shows (0..200%): higher gives more resonant low-end bump.
Amp.Preamp Presence: Undocumented: likely a presence (treble) control in the preamp of amps that have one there.
Amp.Master Bias Excursion: Scales all other bias excursion parameters at once (default usually 100%): higher gives more overall sag and compression.
Amp.High Cut 3: Hi-Cut knob (0..10) on Class-A style amps: higher darkens the tone.
Amp.Power Amp Modeling: ON simulates the power amp; OFF for a real tube power amp, making Master a plain volume and disabling Depth.
Amp.Speaker Breakup: Attack of speaker breakup: SOFT is muted (blues/jazz), MEDIUM normal (rock), HARD tight (modern metal).
Amp.Speaker Thump: Speaker's nonlinear subsonic kick: 5.0 is an amp into a speaker of equal power rating, 2.5 (reset) half that; higher adds thump.
Amp.Plate Suppr. Diodes: Plate suppressor (flyback) diodes: ON reduces upper harmonics and fizz; set per model (e.g. Trainwreck Express).
Amp.Global MV: Second master on some models (e.g. JS410): transparent level into the power amp, unlike the channel master that also cuts highs.
When ON, the Speaker Imp. Curve automatically follows the Cab block's DynaCab type.
Amp.NFB Compensation: ON (default) compensates output volume for negative feedback changes; OFF lets volume change with Negative Feedback.

Delay.Mix: Wet echo level: the dry stays at unity until 50% while the wet rises to full; above 50% the dry fades out. Raise for louder echoes.
Delay.Level: Overall output level of the block (wet and dry); raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Delay.Balance: Left/right balance of the block's output, wet and dry; moving one way makes the opposite side quieter.
Delay.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages fully; MUTE FX IN mutes the effect input so echo tails ring out, the usual choice for delays in series.
Delay.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel out of scene control so scenes no longer change its bypass or channel; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Delay.Kill Dry: ON mutes the dry signal so only echoes pass; use when the block sits on a parallel row and set wet level with Mix.
Delay.Model: Delay type preset (Digital, Analog, Tape, BBD, Ping-Pong, Ducking, 2290 etc.) that sets the block's parameters for that classic echo sound.
Delay.Type: Base delay algorithm (mono, stereo, ping-pong, dual, reverse, sweep, tape, surround); Model sets defaults, this sets the engine.
Delay.Time: Delay time in ms between the note and its echo; longer for spacious leads, short (60-150 ms) for slapback. Ignored when Tempo is set.
Delay.L/R Time Ratio: Right delay time as a % of the left; 100% equal, just below 100% widens, 75% or 50% makes syncopated rhythms.
Delay.Feedback: Amount of echo fed back to set the number of repeats; raise for more repeats, negative values phase-invert the loop.
Delay.Feedl: Left-channel feedback in stereo and Dual Delay types (L->L in Dual); raise for more left repeats, negative values invert phase.
Delay.Feedback R: Right-channel feedback in stereo/dual types; raise for more right repeats. Auto-adjusts with L/R Time Ratio to keep tails balanced.
Delay.Echo Pan: Places the echoes in the stereo field without moving the dry signal; move left or right off centre.
Delay.Spread: Stereo width of the echoes: 100% hard-panned, 0% mono centre, negative swaps sides; lower for a narrower image.
Delay.Tempo: Locks the delay time to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Time value.
Delay.Low Cut Frequency: High-pass on the echoes only; raise to thin out muddy repeats (e.g. 100-300 Hz) while the dry stays full.
Delay.High Cut Frequency: Low-pass on the echoes only; lower it (e.g. 2-4 kHz) for darker analog/tape-style repeats that sit behind the guitar.
Delay.Rate: Speed of LFO 1, which modulates the delay time; raise for faster chorus-like wobble on the repeats.
Delay.Rate 2: Speed of LFO 2, which modulates the delay time; raise for faster wobble, e.g. tape flutter above 6 Hz.
Delay.Depth: Depth of LFO 1 delay-time modulation, scaled by LFO Depth Range; raise for more pitch wobble on the echoes.
Delay.Depth 2: Depth of LFO 2 delay-time modulation, scaled by LFO Depth Range; raise for more pitch wobble on the echoes.
Delay.Drive: Distortion in the delay path, like an overloaded tape or analog delay; raise for grittier repeats, which also get quieter.
Delay.Input Gain: Amount of signal fed into the delay, not the dry; lower it for quieter echoes or cut it to let tails fade naturally.
Delay.Type 2: Waveform of LFO 1 (delay-time modulation); pitch follows the LFO's slope, so TRIANGLE gives a stepped, square-like two-pitch warble.
Delay.Type 3: Waveform of LFO 2 (delay-time modulation); pitch follows the LFO's slope, so TRIANGLE gives a stepped, square-like two-pitch warble.
Delay.Time R: Right delay time in ms for the Dual Delay, independent of the left; set different from Time for wide or rhythmic echoes.
Delay.Repeat Stack/Hold: HOLD mutes the input and loops the current repeats indefinitely; STACK keeps the loop and layers new playing; OFF is normal.
Delay.Master Feedback: Scales every feedback control, 0-200%; above 100% the repeats build into runaway oscillation, so lower to tame them.
Delay.Tempo R: Locks the Dual Delay right time to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Time R value.
Delay.Rotation: Dual Delay cross-feedback from left into right (L->R); as Surround Delay's Rotation, 100% turns each echo 180 degrees and negative reverses.
Delay.Feedrl: Dual Delay cross-feedback from the right line into the left; raise to bounce repeats between the two delays.
Delay.Level 2: Output level of the first delay line or tape head (Dual Delay left, Mono Tape head 1); lower to quieten that echo.
Delay.Level 3: Output level of the second delay line or tape head (Dual Delay right, Mono Tape head 2); lower to quieten that echo.
Delay.Pan: Stereo position of the first delay line or tape head's echoes (Dual Delay left, Mono Tape head 1).
Delay.Pan 2: Stereo position of the second delay line or tape head's echoes (Dual Delay right, Mono Tape head 2).
Delay.Phase: LFO 1 phase offset on the right delay line; raise toward 180 for wider stereo modulation. No effect on mono types.
Delay.Phase 2: LFO 2 phase offset on the right delay line; raise toward 180 for wider stereo modulation. No effect on mono types.
Delay.Crossfade Time: Reverse Delay: overlaps and crossfades the backward snippets; raise for smoother, less choppy reverse playback.
Delay.Run: Reverse Delay: ON plays the reversed audio; OFF mutes playback while recording continues in the background.
Delay.Trigger Restart: Reverse Delay: ON restarts recording when Run turns on, so reversed phrases line up with when you start playing.
Delay.High Cut Slope: Steepness of the echo high cut; steeper (24-36 dB/oct) gives the narrow, dark bandwidth of vintage analog delays.
Delay.Attenuation: Ducker: how much the echoes drop while you play above the threshold, e.g. 20 dB; 0 turns ducking off.
Delay.Threshold: Ducker: input level above which echoes are ducked; lower it so ducking kicks in at softer playing.
Delay.Release Time: Ducker: how fast echoes swell back after you stop playing; short returns at once, longer swells back gradually.
Delay.Diffusion: Mix of the diffuser that smears the repeats into a reverb-like wash; 10-20% softens echoes, higher sounds like reverb.
Delay.Diffusion Time: Time of the diffuser that smears the repeats; raise for a longer, more reverb-like smear.
Delay.Phase Reverse: Phase-inverts the LEFT, RIGHT or BOTH delay outputs; RIGHT can make echoes vanish if the signal is later summed to mono.
Delay.Target: Which delay line LFO 1 modulates: LEFT, RIGHT or BOTH; mono types only use the left line.
Delay.Target 2: Which delay line LFO 2 modulates: LEFT, RIGHT or BOTH; mono types only use the left line.
Delay.Tempo 2: Locks the LFO 1 rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Rate value.
Delay.Tempo 3: Locks the LFO 2 rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Rate 2 value.
Delay.Sweep Rate: Sweep Delay: speed of the LFO sweeping the bandpass filter on the echoes; raise for faster sweeps.
Delay.Sweep Type: Sweep Delay: waveform of the LFO sweeping the bandpass filter on the echoes.
Delay.Sweep Phase: Sweep Delay: phase of the right channel's sweep LFO; raise above zero for stereo sweeps.
Delay.Sweep Tempo: Locks the Sweep Delay filter sweep to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Sweep Rate value.
Delay.Start Frequency: Sweep Delay: one end of the bandpass filter's sweep range; with Stop Frequency it sets how wide the sweep is.
Delay.Stop Frequency: Sweep Delay: other end of the bandpass filter's sweep range; with Start Frequency it sets how wide the sweep is.
Delay.Resonance: Sweep Delay: resonance of the sweeping filter; raise for a more intense, vocal sweep on the echoes.
Delay.Q (High+Low): Resonance of the low and high cut filters when their slope is above 6 dB/oct; raise for a peak at the cutoff.
Delay.Bit Reduction: Bits removed from 24-bit for lo-fi vintage digital echoes, e.g. 8 gives 16-bit; raise for grittier repeats.
Delay.Freq 1: Centre frequency of the low-range (20 Hz-2 kHz) peaking EQ on the echoes; pair with Gain 1 to boost or cut there.
Delay.Freq 2: Centre frequency of the high-range (100 Hz-10 kHz) peaking EQ on the echoes; pair with Gain 2 to boost or cut there.
Delay.Q 1: Bandwidth of echo EQ band 1; raise for a narrower boost or cut.
Delay.Q 2: Bandwidth of echo EQ band 2; raise for a narrower boost or cut.
Delay.Gain 1: Boost or cut of echo EQ band 1 at Freq 1, in dB; affects only the repeats.
Delay.Gain 2: Boost or cut of echo EQ band 2 at Freq 2, in dB; affects only the repeats.
Delay.LFO Depth Range: Overall range of delay-time modulation for LFO 1 and 2: LOW for subtle chorus, HIGH for deep warble.
Delay.Motor Speed: Tape types: tape speed, 0.5-2x; faster shortens the delay time, slower lengthens it, and changes in real time warp the pitch.
Delay.Right Post Delay: Adds 0-100 ms of extra delay to the right wet output to widen a mono echo; raise for a wider image.
Delay.Low Cut Slope: Steepness of the echo low cut; steeper removes lows more sharply below the cutoff.
Delay.Compander: ON compresses into and expands out of the delay line like BBD pedals, for lower noise and softer transients; disables Stack/Hold.
Delay.Time 2: Undocumented: likely the compander time constant, which shapes how echo transients are softened.
Delay.Threshold 2: Compander detection threshold (default -60 dB, like an NE570); raise it for a more prominent softening of the echo transients.
Delay.Master Time: Undocumented: likely scales all delay times by 25-400%; raise for longer echoes without changing each time.
Delay.LFO Rate: Speed of the diffuser modulation, adding chorus-like movement to the diffused echoes.
Delay.LFO Depth: Depth of the diffuser modulation; raise for more chorus-like movement in the diffused echoes.
Delay.Type 4: Waveform of LFO 3, which modulates the echoes' level, pan or spread (per Target 3); sets the shape of that tremolo or auto-pan movement.
Delay.Rate 3: Speed of LFO 3, which modulates the echoes' level, pan or spread (per Target 3) for vintage-digital tremolo or auto-pan.
Delay.Tempo 4: Locks the LFO 3 rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Rate 3 value.
Delay.Depth 3: Depth of LFO 3 level, pan or spread modulation; raise for stronger tremolo or panning of the echoes.
Delay.Phase 3: LFO 3 phase offset on the right channel; raise toward 180 for stereo movement.
Delay.Target 3: What LFO 3 modulates on the echoes: NONE, LEVEL (tremolo), PAN (auto-pan) or SPREAD (width).
Delay.Stack Feedback: Decay of repeats while Stack/Hold is on STACK; lower so stacked layers fade, maximum for near-infinite sustain.
Delay.Hold Feedback: Decay of repeats while Stack/Hold is on HOLD; lower so the held loop fades, maximum for near-infinite sustain.
Delay.Filter Type: Undocumented: likely the response of the Sweep Delay's swept filter: lowpass, bandpass or highpass.
Delay.Dry Diffusion: Diffuses the dry signal apart from the wet Diffusion, smearing pick attack like a short ambience; any diffusion here costs CPU.

Multitap Delay.Algorithm: Core engine (Quad-Tap, Parallel, Series, Diffusor, Tape, Tap Band) without resetting other parameters; try alternatives on the same settings.
Multitap Delay.Delay 1: Time in ms at which tap 1 is heard; set with the other taps to build the echo rhythm. Ignored when Tempo 1 is set.
Multitap Delay.Delay 2: Time in ms at which tap 2 is heard; set with the other taps to build the echo rhythm. Ignored when Tempo 2 is set.
Multitap Delay.Delay 3: Time in ms at which tap 3 is heard; set with the other taps to build the echo rhythm. Ignored when Tempo 3 is set.
Multitap Delay.Delay 4: Time in ms at which tap 4 is heard; set with the other taps to build the echo rhythm. Ignored when Tempo 4 is set.
Multitap Delay.Tempo 1: Locks tap 1's time to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Delay 1 value.
Multitap Delay.Tempo 2: Locks tap 2's time to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Delay 2 value.
Multitap Delay.Tempo 3: Locks tap 3's time to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Delay 3 value.

Multitap Delay.Level 3: Output level of tap 3 in the mix; lower to soften that echo, negative values also invert its phase.

Multitap Delay.Pan 2: Stereo position of tap 2; spread taps across left and right for wide, moving echo patterns.
Multitap Delay.Pan 3: Stereo position of tap 3; spread taps across left and right for wide, moving echo patterns.
Multitap Delay.Pan 4: Stereo position of tap 4; spread taps across left and right for wide, moving echo patterns.
Multitap Delay.LFO 1 Rate: Speed of LFO 1, which modulates the tap delay times; raise for faster chorus-like wobble.
Multitap Delay.LFO 2 Rate: Speed of LFO 2, which modulates the tap delay times; raise for faster chorus-like wobble.
Multitap Delay.LFO 1 Depth: Depth of LFO 1 delay-time modulation; raise for more pitch wobble on the taps.
Multitap Delay.LFO 2 Depth: Depth of LFO 2 delay-time modulation; raise for more pitch wobble on the taps.
Multitap Delay.LFO 1 Type: Waveform of LFO 1, which modulates the tap delay times.
Multitap Delay.LFO 2 Type: Waveform of LFO 2, which modulates the tap delay times.

Multitap Delay.LFO 2 Tempo: Locks LFO 2's rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual LFO 2 Rate value.
Multitap Delay.LFO 1 Phase: LFO 1 phase of tap 2 relative to tap 1 (taps 3 and 4 are inverted); 90 spreads the taps evenly for lush stereo movement.
Multitap Delay.LFO 2 Phase: LFO 2 phase of tap 2 relative to tap 1 (taps 3 and 4 are inverted); 90 spreads the taps evenly for lush stereo movement.
Multitap Delay.Mix: Balance of wet echoes and dry signal; raise for louder echoes, 100% for wet only on a parallel row.
Multitap Delay.Level: Overall output level of the block (wet and dry); raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Multitap Delay.Balance: Left/right balance of the block's output, wet and dry; moving one way makes the opposite side quieter.
Multitap Delay.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages fully; MUTE FX IN mutes the effect input so echo tails ring out, the usual choice for delays in series.
Multitap Delay.Input Gain: Amount of signal fed into the delay, not the dry; lower it for quieter echoes or cut it to let tails fade naturally.
Multitap Delay.Diffusion Mix: Level of the diffuser that adds a reverb-like smear to the taps; raise to blur echoes toward reverb.
Multitap Delay.Diffusion Time: Time of the diffuser that smears the taps; raise for a longer, more reverb-like smear.
Multitap Delay.Threshold: Ducker: input level above which echoes are ducked; lower it so ducking kicks in at softer playing.
Multitap Delay.Time: Master Time: scales the times of all taps (or all four diffusors); lower for tighter echoes, very low turns echoes into reverb.
Multitap Delay.Level 5: Master Level: scales the output levels of all taps; lower to quieten every echo together.
Multitap Delay.Pan: Master Pan: scales all tap pans as a width control; lower to narrow, negative swaps left and right.
Multitap Delay.Filter Frequency: Master Filter Frequency: scales the centre frequency of all tap bandpass filters; raise for brighter taps.
Multitap Delay.Filter Q: Master Filter Q: scales the bandwidth of all tap bandpass filters; minimum disables them, high Q gives extreme, resonant taps.
Multitap Delay.Feedback: Master Feedback: scales feedback for all taps, setting overall density; raise for more repeats.
Multitap Delay.LFO Rate: Master LFO Rate: scales the rate of all LFOs; raise for faster modulation everywhere.
Multitap Delay.LFO Depth: Master LFO Depth: scales the depth of all LFOs; raise for deeper modulation everywhere.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 1: Centre frequency of the bandpass filter on tap 1, inside the feedback loop; lower for darker, raise for thinner echoes.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 2: Centre frequency of the bandpass filter on tap 2, inside the feedback loop; lower for darker, raise for thinner echoes.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 3: Centre frequency of the bandpass filter on tap 3, inside the feedback loop; lower for darker, raise for thinner echoes.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 4: Centre frequency of the bandpass filter on tap 4, inside the feedback loop; lower for darker, raise for thinner echoes.
Multitap Delay.Q 1: Bandwidth of tap 1's bandpass filter; higher Q is narrower and boosts gain, so watch for runaway feedback.
Multitap Delay.Q 2: Bandwidth of tap 2's bandpass filter; higher Q is narrower and boosts gain, so watch for runaway feedback.
Multitap Delay.Q 3: Bandwidth of tap 3's bandpass filter; higher Q is narrower and boosts gain, so watch for runaway feedback.
Multitap Delay.Q 4: Bandwidth of tap 4's bandpass filter; higher Q is narrower and boosts gain, so watch for runaway feedback.
Multitap Delay.Attenuation: Ducker: how much the echoes drop while you play above the threshold, e.g. 20 dB; 0 turns ducking off.
Multitap Delay.Motor Speed: Tape types: tape speed; faster shortens the tap times, slower lengthens them, and real-time changes warp the pitch.
Multitap Delay.Low Cut: High-pass on the echoes only; raise to thin out muddy repeats while the dry stays full.
Multitap Delay.High Cut: Low-pass on the echoes only; lower it for darker, vintage-style repeats.
Multitap Delay.Feedback 5: Quad Series Delay: total feedback from the chosen send tap back to the input; raise for more repeats.
Multitap Delay.Release Time: Ducker: how fast echoes swell back after you stop playing; short returns at once, longer swells back gradually.
Multitap Delay.Drive: Distortion added to the echoes for saturation; raise for grittier repeats.
Multitap Delay.Rate: Speed of the LFO that sweeps the four tap bandpass filters; raise for faster filter movement.
Multitap Delay.Depth: Depth of the LFO that sweeps the four tap bandpass filters; raise for more pronounced filter movement.
Multitap Delay.Type: Waveform of the LFO that sweeps the four tap bandpass filters.
Multitap Delay.Tempo: Locks the filter LFO rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Rate value.
Multitap Delay.Phase: Filter LFO phase of filter 2 relative to filter 1 (3 and 4 inverted); raise for stereo-spread filter movement.
Multitap Delay.Threshold 2: Envelope follower threshold for volume swells; try -70 dB with about 400 ms attack and 15 ms release.
Multitap Delay.Attack Time: Envelope follower fade-in time for swells; raise for slower, more ambient volume roll-ups (about 400 ms is typical).
Multitap Delay.Release Time 2: Envelope follower release time; about 15 ms suits basic volume swells.
Multitap Delay.Comb Time: Master Comb Time: scales the times of the four comb filters (Parallel and Series types).
Multitap Delay.Comb Feedback: Master Comb Depth: scales comb filter feedback; raise above 0% to hear the comb filters at all.
Multitap Delay.Filter Type: Undocumented: likely selects feedback or feedforward comb filtering for the Parallel and Series comb filters.
Multitap Delay.Time 2: Comb filter time for delay voice 1 (0-40 ms); changes the metallic pitch of the comb colouring.
Multitap Delay.Time 3: Comb filter time for delay voice 2 (0-40 ms); changes the metallic pitch of the comb colouring.
Multitap Delay.Time 4: Comb filter time for delay voice 3 (0-40 ms); changes the metallic pitch of the comb colouring.
Multitap Delay.Time 5: Comb filter time for delay voice 4 (0-40 ms); changes the metallic pitch of the comb colouring.
Multitap Delay.Feedback 6: Comb filter feedback for delay voice 1; raise for a stronger, more resonant comb effect.
Multitap Delay.Feedback 7: Comb filter feedback for delay voice 2; raise for a stronger, more resonant comb effect.
Multitap Delay.Feedback 8: Comb filter feedback for delay voice 3; raise for a stronger, more resonant comb effect.
Multitap Delay.Feedback 9: Comb filter feedback for delay voice 4; raise for a stronger, more resonant comb effect.
Multitap Delay.Ring Mod Frequency: Master Ring Mod Frequency: scales the ring modulator frequencies on all voices.
Multitap Delay.Ring Mod Mix: Master Ring Mod Mix: scales ring modulation on all voices; 0 defeats the ring mods, raise for strange metallic echoes.
Multitap Delay.Frequency: Ring modulator frequency for delay voice 1; changes the clangorous, metallic pitch of that echo.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 5: Ring modulator frequency for delay voice 2; changes the clangorous, metallic pitch of that echo.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 6: Ring modulator frequency for delay voice 3; changes the clangorous, metallic pitch of that echo.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 7: Ring modulator frequency for delay voice 4; changes the clangorous, metallic pitch of that echo.
Multitap Delay.Mix 2: Ring modulator mix for delay voice 1; raise for more metallic ring-mod character on that echo.
Multitap Delay.Mix 3: Ring modulator mix for delay voice 2; raise for more metallic ring-mod character on that echo.
Multitap Delay.Mix 4: Ring modulator mix for delay voice 3; raise for more metallic ring-mod character on that echo.
Multitap Delay.Mix 5: Ring modulator mix for delay voice 4; raise for more metallic ring-mod character on that echo.
Multitap Delay.Rate 2: Chorus LFO rate for delay voice 1; with short tap times (2-20 ms) the taps act as independent choruses.
Multitap Delay.Rate 3: Chorus LFO rate for delay voice 2; with short tap times (2-20 ms) the taps act as independent choruses.
Multitap Delay.Rate 4: Chorus LFO rate for delay voice 3; with short tap times (2-20 ms) the taps act as independent choruses.
Multitap Delay.Rate 5: Chorus LFO rate for delay voice 4; with short tap times (2-20 ms) the taps act as independent choruses.
Multitap Delay.Depth 2: Chorus LFO depth for delay voice 1; raise for a deeper, lusher chorus on that voice.
Multitap Delay.Depth 3: Chorus LFO depth for delay voice 2; raise for a deeper, lusher chorus on that voice.
Multitap Delay.Depth 4: Chorus LFO depth for delay voice 3; raise for a deeper, lusher chorus on that voice.
Multitap Delay.Depth 5: Chorus LFO depth for delay voice 4; raise for a deeper, lusher chorus on that voice.
Multitap Delay.Input Select: Which input feeds the effect: L+R sums stereo (default), or LEFT or RIGHT only.
Multitap Delay.Chorus Rate: Master Chorus Rate: scales the chorus rate of all four voices.
Multitap Delay.Chorus Depth: Master Chorus Depth: scales the chorus depth of all four voices; raise for lusher chorusing.
Multitap Delay.Type 2: Type of the single multi-mode filter on the echoes (lowpass, bandpass, shelf, peaking, notch, tilt); NULL turns it off.
Multitap Delay.Frequency 8: Frequency of the multi-mode echo filter; move to where you want to cut or boost the repeats.
Multitap Delay.Q: Bandwidth or resonance of the multi-mode echo filter; raise for a narrower, more pronounced effect.
Multitap Delay.Gain: Boost or cut of the multi-mode echo filter for shelf and peaking types, in dB.
Multitap Delay.Low Cut Slope: Steepness of the echo low cut; steeper removes lows more sharply.
Multitap Delay.High Cut Slope: Steepness of the echo high cut; steeper gives a darker, more vintage bandwidth.
Multitap Delay.LFO Rate 2: Speed of the diffuser modulation, adding chorus-like movement to the diffused echoes.
Multitap Delay.LFO Depth 2: Depth of the diffuser modulation; raise for more chorus-like movement in the diffused echoes.

Multitap Delay.Feedback41: Quad Parallel types: cross-feedback from voice 4 into voice 1; raise for interwoven repeats, negative inverts phase.

Ten-Tap Delay.Type: Ten-Tap Delay sets evenly spaced taps by one time; Rhythm Tap Delay lets each tap have its own time for custom rhythms.
Ten-Tap Delay.Mono / Stereo: Mono or stereo operation; mono allows twice as much delay per tap, stereo enables Spread and Ratio.
Ten-Tap Delay.Subdiv: Undocumented: likely a rhythmic subdivision used for tap spacing in the Rhythm Tap Delay.
Ten-Tap Delay.Quantize: Rhythm Tap: length of each rhythmic div that tap times snap to (e.g. 1/16); NONE sets tap times in ms.
Ten-Tap Delay.Decay: How fast the taps get quieter over time; 0% keeps all taps equal, raise for a quicker fade.
Ten-Tap Delay.Decaystyle: Undocumented: likely selects the shape of the tap level decay curve.
Ten-Tap Delay.Shuffle: Time offset on the odd-numbered taps for a swung, shuffle feel; raise for more swing.
Ten-Tap Delay.Delay Tempo: Locks the time between taps to a note value of the preset tempo; set NONE for manual time.
Ten-Tap Delay.Spread: Stereo mode: width of the repeats; maximum pans left fully left and right fully right.
Ten-Tap Delay.Pan Shape: How the taps move across the stereo field: CONSTANT, INCREASING or DECREASING sweeps, UP/DOWN, DOWN/UP or SINE back and forth.
Ten-Tap Delay.Pan Alpha: How quickly taps move per Pan Shape; raise for a stronger effect; SINE at maximum alternates left and right.
Ten-Tap Delay.Low Cut: High-pass on the repeats; raise to thin them out.
Ten-Tap Delay.High Cut: Low-pass on the repeats; lower for darker echoes.
Ten-Tap Delay.Ratio: Stereo mode: left time as a percentage of the right; below 100% offsets the sides for a wider or rhythmic image.
Ten-Tap Delay.Feedback: Rhythm Tap: feeds the last repeat back to the input so the whole tap pattern repeats; raise for more pattern repeats.
Ten-Tap Delay.Level 1: Level of tap 1, -80 to +20 dB; shape custom echo patterns alongside or instead of Decay.

Plex Delay.Input Gain: Amount of signal fed into the delay, not the dry; lower it for quieter echoes or cut it to let tails fade naturally.
Plex Delay.Time: Master Time: scales all delay times; lower for tighter, denser echoes, raise for longer ones.
Plex Delay.Level: Master Level: scales the output levels of all delay lines.
Plex Delay.Pan: Master Pan: scales all pans as a width control; lower to narrow, negative swaps left and right.
Plex Delay.Pitch: Undocumented: likely a master scale for all Shift amounts, like Master Detune does for Detune.
Plex Delay.Detune: Master Detune: scales all eight Detune amounts; raise for more detuning, negative inverts them.
Plex Delay.Decay Time: How long the echoes take to fade, like feedback; raise for longer tails, but very high values can become unstable.
Plex Delay.Diffusion: Cross-feedback in the delay matrix; raise for a denser, smoother, more reverb-like sound.
Plex Delay.Direction: Pitch-shifter granules play FORWARD or REVERSE; REVERSE gives backwards-sounding shifted echoes.
Plex Delay.Granule Length: Length of the pitch-shifter granules; lower sounds grainy, higher sounds smooth and blended.
Plex Delay.Low Cut: Gentle high-pass in the matrix; raise to thin the tail (around 250 Hz for pad-like Plex Verb sounds).
Plex Delay.High Cut: Gentle low-pass in the matrix; lower for a darker tail (around 2 kHz for pad-like Plex Verb sounds).
Plex Delay.Attenuation: Ducker: how much the effect drops while you play above the threshold, e.g. 20 dB; 0 turns ducking off.
Plex Delay.Threshold: Ducker: input level above which the effect is ducked; lower it so ducking kicks in at softer playing.
Plex Delay.Release: Ducker: how fast the effect swells back after you stop playing; longer swells back more gradually.
Plex Delay.Mix: Input diffuser level, smearing transients before the Plex so individual echoes blur; raise for smoother, verb-like results.
Plex Delay.Time 9: Input diffuser time; raise for a longer smear of transients before the Plex.
Plex Delay.Rate: Speed of the delay modulation LFO, adding chorus-like movement; raise for faster movement.
Plex Delay.Depth: Depth of the delay modulation LFO; raise for more chorusing.
Plex Delay.Tempo: Locks the modulation LFO rate to a note value of the preset tempo, e.g. 1/4 or 1/8 DOT; set NONE to use the manual Rate value.
Plex Delay.Threshold 2: Envelope follower threshold for volume swells; try -70 dB with about 400 ms attack and 15 ms release.
Plex Delay.Attack: Envelope follower fade-in time for swells; raise for slower, more ambient roll-ups (about 400 ms is typical).
Plex Delay.Release 2: Envelope follower release time; about 15 ms suits basic volume swells.
Plex Delay.Mix 2: Balance of wet effect and dry signal; raise for more effect, 100% for wet only on a parallel row.
Plex Delay.Level 9: Overall output level of the block (wet and dry); raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Plex Delay.Balance: Left/right balance of the block's output, wet and dry; moving one way makes the opposite side quieter.
Plex Delay.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages fully; MUTE FX IN mutes the effect input so echo tails ring out, the usual choice for delays in series.
Plex Delay.Reverb Size: Plex Verb and Shimmer Verb: how long echoes take to bounce between virtual surfaces; raise for a bigger space.
Plex Delay.Spread: Stereo width: 100% hard-panned, 0% mono, negative reversed; beyond +/-100% widens past the speakers.
Plex Delay.Pre-Delay: Extra delay before the effect is heard; raise to separate the effect from the attack of the note.
Plex Delay.Type: Type of the filter on the wet signal (lowpass, bandpass, shelf, peaking, notch, tilt); NULL turns it off.
Plex Delay.Frequency: Frequency of the wet-signal filter and one end of its LFO sweep; move to where you want to shape the effect.
Plex Delay.Q: Bandwidth or resonance of the wet-signal filter; raise for a narrower, more pronounced effect.
Plex Delay.Gain: Boost or cut of the wet-signal filter for shelf and peaking types, in dB.
Plex Delay.Shimmer Intensity: Shimmer Verb: amount of upper-octave pitch shift, ten levels; raise for brighter, stronger shimmer.
Plex Delay.Input Select: Which input feeds the effect: L+R sums stereo (default), or LEFT or RIGHT only.
Plex Delay.Stack/Hold: HOLD mutes the input and sustains the current tail indefinitely; STACK sustains it while layering new playing; OFF is normal.
Plex Delay.Presets: Plex type preset (Plex Delay, Shimmer Verb, Golden Shimmer, Reverse Plex and more) that loads that effect's settings.
Plex Delay.LFO Type: Waveform of the LFO that sweeps the wet-signal filter between Frequency and Mod Frequency; OFF disables the sweep.
Plex Delay.LFO Rate: Speed of the LFO sweeping the wet-signal filter; raise for faster filter movement.
Plex Delay.Mod Frequency: Other end of the wet-filter LFO sweep from Frequency; set further away for a wider sweep.
Plex Delay.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel out of scene control so scenes no longer change its bypass or channel; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Plex Delay.Kill Dry: ON mutes the dry signal so only echoes pass; use when the block sits on a parallel row and set wet level with Mix.

Compressor.Threshold: Level above which compression starts (below which upward/sustainer types boost); lower it for more compression.
Compressor.Ratio: How strongly signal over threshold is reduced, e.g. 2:1; raise for heavier squash and less dynamics, keep low for light compression.
Compressor.Attack Time: How fast gain reduction kicks in; faster tames peaks, slower lets pick attack through for punch.
Compressor.Release Time: How fast gain recovers after compression; faster punctuates chugs and chicken pickin', slower is smoother but can hold levels down.
Compressor.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Compressor.Knee Type: How gradually compression engages near the threshold; HARD is abrupt, SOFT is more transparent.
Compressor.Auto Makeup: When ON, raises output to keep perceived loudness at the current threshold and ratio (assumes humbucker-level input).
Compressor.Detector Type: Level detection: RMS smooth, PEAK fast and punchy for guitar, RMS+PEAK both, HALF-WAVE alters attack/release and adds grit.
Compressor.Low Cut: Highpass on the detector signal; raise it so low thumps trigger less compression and pumping.
Compressor.Sidechain Source: Signal feeding the detector: BLOCK L+R is the block input (normal); rows or inputs key it externally; BLOCK L/R suit after out-of-phase FX.
Compressor.Mix: Wet (compressed) vs dry balance; normally 100%, lower for parallel (New York) compression that keeps pick attack.
Compressor.Type: Compressor model: studio VCA, JFET, optical, vari-mu tube, pedal comps, sustainers (upward), compander; each has its own feel and controls.
Compressor.Compression: Ratio-like amount control on pedal-style types; raise for more squash and sustain.
Compressor.Bypass Mode: When bypassed: THRU disengages the block, MUTE FX OUT mutes the effect but keeps dry, MUTE OUT silences the output.
Compressor.Look-Ahead Time: Delays the audio so the detector catches the fastest transients; adds latency, so leave at 0 unless peaks slip through.
Compressor.Auto Att/Rel: When ON, faster transients get faster attack/release times, helping avoid pumping with varied playing.
Compressor.Emphasis: High-shelf boost on the detector (opto: Limiter Response) so lows drive compression less; raise to reduce thumpy low-end pumping.
Compressor.Dynamics: Dynamics Processor only: below zero compresses (flatter dynamics), above zero expands (exaggerated dynamics, quiet parts quieter).
Compressor.Input Level: Detector optimisation: INSTRUMENT for guitar level before the amp, LINE when the block is after the amp.
Compressor.High Cut: Lowpass on the detector signal; lower it so pick chirps and highs trigger less compression.
Compressor.Gain: Boost or cut of the variable detector filter; boost makes that band trigger more compression, cut makes it trigger less.
Compressor.Frequency: Frequency of the variable detector filter, choosing which part of the spectrum the compressor responds to more or less.
Compressor.Q: Bandwidth of the variable detector filter; higher values make it narrower.
Compressor.Filter Type: Shape of the variable sidechain (detector) filter used to boost or cut what the compressor responds to; NULL disables it.
Compressor.Threshold 2: Undocumented: a second compressor threshold (COMP_THRESH2) used by some types; Fractal's docs do not say which types or how it acts.
Compressor.Ratio 2: Compander type's Ratio: how hard its compressor-then-expander pair works; raise for stronger compansion, then use Transients to soften or add pick attack.
Compressor.Time: Compander time constant for its compressor/expander pair; sets how quickly the compander responds.
Compressor.Transients: Compander transient shaping: below zero softens and smooths pick attack, above zero emphasises attack and punch.
Compressor.Emphasis Frequency: Shifts the frequency range of the Emphasis detector curve.
Compressor.Scene Ignore: When ON the block ignores scene changes and keeps its current state; leave OFF for normal scene control.
Compressor.Tone: Dynami-Comp and Citrus Juicer types: the pedal-style Tone control (as on Dyna Comp clones), shaping how bright the compressed sound is.
Compressor.Drive: Overdrives the output stage (OTA on Dynami-Comp types) for saturation; raise for more grit and distortion.

Multiband Compressor.Crossover: Frequency dividing the low and mid bands; raise it to put more low mids into the low band.
Multiband Compressor.Crossover 2: Frequency dividing the mid and high bands; lower it to put more upper mids into the high band.
Multiband Compressor.Threshold: Threshold above which the low band is compressed; lower it for more compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Ratio: Input:output ratio of the low band above threshold (2 = 2:1); raise for heavier compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Attack: How fast the low band compresses once over threshold; higher lets more pick attack pop through.
Multiband Compressor.Release: How fast the low band recovers; too fast with fast attack and heavy ratio distorts, slower holds the level down longer.
Multiband Compressor.Level: Output level of the low band; raise or lower to rebalance that band, like a dynamic EQ.
Multiband Compressor.Detector: Detection for the low band: RMS is smooth for evening out, PEAK is fast for limiting guitar spikes.
Multiband Compressor.Mute: MUTE silences the low band; mute two bands to solo the third while setting up, OFF in normal use.
Multiband Compressor.Threshold 2: Threshold above which the mid band is compressed; lower it for more compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Ratio 2: Input:output ratio of the mid band above threshold (2 = 2:1); raise for heavier compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Attack 2: How fast the mid band compresses once over threshold; higher lets more pick attack pop through.
Multiband Compressor.Release 2: How fast the mid band recovers; too fast with fast attack and heavy ratio distorts, slower holds the level down longer.
Multiband Compressor.Level 2: Output level of the mid band; raise or lower to rebalance that band, like a dynamic EQ.
Multiband Compressor.Detector 2: Detection for the mid band: RMS is smooth for evening out, PEAK is fast for limiting guitar spikes.
Multiband Compressor.Mute 2: MUTE silences the mid band; mute two bands to solo the third while setting up, OFF in normal use.
Multiband Compressor.Threshold 3: Threshold above which the high band is compressed; lower it for more compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Ratio 3: Input:output ratio of the high band above threshold (2 = 2:1); raise for heavier compression of that band.
Multiband Compressor.Attack 3: How fast the high band compresses once over threshold; higher lets more pick attack pop through.
Multiband Compressor.Release 3: How fast the high band recovers; too fast with fast attack and heavy ratio distorts, slower holds the level down longer.
Multiband Compressor.Level 3: Output level of the high band; raise or lower to rebalance that band, like a dynamic EQ.
Multiband Compressor.Detector 3: Detection for the high band: RMS is smooth for evening out, PEAK is fast for limiting guitar spikes.
Multiband Compressor.Mute 3: MUTE silences the high band; mute two bands to solo the third while setting up, OFF in normal use.
Multiband Compressor.Mix: Wet (compressed) vs dry balance; normally 100%, lower for parallel compression.
Multiband Compressor.Level 4: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Multiband Compressor.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving toward one side makes the opposite channel quieter.
Multiband Compressor.Bypass Mode: When bypassed: THRU disengages the block, MUTE FX OUT mutes the effect but keeps the dry signal.
Multiband Compressor.Crossover Slope: Steepness of the band-splitting filters: 12 dB/oct overlaps bands more, 24 dB/oct separates them more sharply.
Multiband Compressor.Knee Type: How abruptly compression begins near the threshold; HARD is abrupt, SOFT is gentler and more transparent.
Multiband Compressor.Auto Att/Rel: When ON, attack and release times are optimised automatically from the playing.
Multiband Compressor.Scene Ignore: When ON the block ignores scene changes and keeps its current state; leave OFF for normal scene control.

Graphic EQ.Band 1: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 1 (31 Hz on 10 Band types, a low shelf); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 2: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 2 (63 Hz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 3: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 3 (125 Hz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 4: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 4 (250 Hz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 5: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 5 (500 Hz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 6: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 6 (1 kHz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 7: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 7 (2 kHz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 8: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 8 (4 kHz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 9: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 9 (8 kHz on 10 Band types); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Band 10: Boost (+) or cut (-) up to 12 dB at band 10 (16 kHz on 10 Band types, a high shelf); frequencies and band count change with Type.
Graphic EQ.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Graphic EQ.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving toward one side makes the opposite channel quieter.
Graphic EQ.Bypass Mode: What happens when bypassed: THRU passes the signal as if the block were absent, MUTE silences it.
Graphic EQ.Type: Band count and behaviour: constant or variable Q graphics, pedal (7/8 band), passive, console, Mark or JMP-1 style; outer bands are shelves.
Graphic EQ.Master Q: Bandwidth of all bands: 1.0 is default (about one octave), lower widens and overlaps bands, higher narrows and focuses each band.
Graphic EQ.Scene Ignore: When ON the block ignores scene changes and keeps its current state; leave OFF for normal scene control.

Volume/Pan.Volume: Scales the block's output from 0 (silent) to 10 (full); assign a modifier to make a volume pedal.
Volume/Pan.Balance: Left/right output balance of the block.
Volume/Pan.Volume Taper: Response curve of Volume: LINEAR, LOG pot tapers (30A to 5A) like real volume pots, or S-TAPER designed for swells.
Volume/Pan.Pan Left: Pan position of the left output signal; -100 is hard left, +100 hard right.
Volume/Pan.Pan Right: Pan position of the right output signal; -100 is hard left, +100 hard right.
Volume/Pan.Level: Output level in dB independent of Volume; use as a static boost or cut.
Volume/Pan.Bypass Mode: When bypassed: THRU passes the signal unchanged, MUTE silences it.
Volume/Pan.Input Select: Which input passes: STEREO, LEFT ONLY or RIGHT ONLY, for isolating one channel.
Volume/Pan.Type: VOLUME is a plain volume control; AUTO-SWELL (slow gear style) fades in each note like rolling up the guitar volume knob.
Volume/Pan.Threshold: Auto-Swell: input level that triggers a swell; lower it to trigger on softer playing.
Volume/Pan.Attack: Auto-Swell: volume roll-up speed of each note; raise for slower, longer swells.
Volume/Pan.Release: Auto-Swell release time, added to fine-tune swells to playing style; Fractal gives no further detail.
Volume/Pan.Hysteresis: Auto-Swell detector hysteresis, added to fine-tune swell triggering to playing style; Fractal gives no further detail.

Enhancer.Width: Stereo widening amount: Modern shapes the separation, Classic delays the right channel 0-20 ms (35% = 7 ms); raise for wider.
Enhancer.Depth: Modern/Stereoizer: how far opposing frequency bands spread left and right; raise for a wider image.
Enhancer.Low Cut: Modern: frequencies below this pass unwidened; raise it to keep the low end centred.
Enhancer.High Cut: Modern: frequencies above this pass unwidened; lower it to leave more highs unaffected.
Enhancer.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Enhancer.Type: Modern (frequency split) and Stereoizer (high-order filters) are mono-safe; Classic delays one side and can phase when summed to mono.
Enhancer.Phase Invert: Classic: inverts the phase of the left, right or both channels; use with Width to change the apparent widening.
Enhancer.Pan Left: Classic: pan position of the left output; with Pan Right it can narrow, merge to mono or swap channels.
Enhancer.Pan Right: Classic: pan position of the right output; with Pan Left it can narrow, merge to mono or swap channels.
Enhancer.Balance: Relative left/right output volume; use it to offset the Classic type's apparent shift away from the delayed side.
Enhancer.Scene Ignore: When ON the block ignores scene changes and keeps its current state; leave OFF for normal scene control.

Chorus.Type: Selects the chorus model (analog BBD, CE-1/CE-2, Dimension, Tri-Chorus, tape, vibrato, etc.) and presets other settings, but not Rate or Depth.
Chorus.Number of Voices: Number of modulated delay lines; more voices sound fuller and lusher, two gives a vintage chorus; above two forces a Sine LFO.
Chorus.Rate: Speed of the chorus sweep; low rates with more depth give slow movement, raise rate and depth toward vibrato.
Chorus.Tempo: Locks Rate to a note value of the preset tempo (1/4 at 120 BPM = 2 Hz); set NONE to use the Rate knob instead.
Chorus.Depth: Amount of delay modulation, i.e. how much detune each voice gets; raise for a wider wobble, usually inversely to Rate.
Chorus.High Cut: Low-pass filter on the processed signal; lower it for a darker, warmer vintage chorus.
Chorus.Delay Time: Minimum delay of the voices; low values sound more singular, higher values approach a fast slapback.
Chorus.LFO Phase: Phase offset between left and right LFOs; 0 for mono (use before the amp), higher for a wider stereo difference.
Chorus.LFO Type: Shape of the modulation waveform; Sine and Triangle are the usual smooth choices, Square/Saw/Random give choppy or stepped motion.
Chorus.Auto Depth: Scales Depth with Rate so the chorus sounds consistent at any speed; turn OFF for precise control or deeper, wilder settings.
Chorus.Mix: Wet/dry balance; 50% is a classic blend (each at -6 dB), raise toward 100% for all-wet effects such as vibrato.
Chorus.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Chorus.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Chorus.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE modes silence all output, or only the effect output while the dry passes.
Chorus.Phase Reverse: Inverts the wet output of the left, right or both channels; can widen the sound but may cancel when summed to mono.
Chorus.Width: Shortens the right delay relative to the left (toward 1 ms at 100%) to widen the stereo image; 0 keeps both sides equal.
Chorus.LFO2 Rate: Speed of the secondary LFO that modulates the main LFO, for more complex, less regular movement.
Chorus.LFO2 Depth: Amount the secondary LFO modulates the main LFO; 0 disables it, raise for more irregular motion.
Chorus.Drive: Simulates the gentle distortion of an overdriven analog bucket-brigade chip; 0 is pristine clean, raise for grit.
Chorus.Low Cut: High-pass filter on the processed signal; raise it to remove bass from the chorus, e.g. for bass guitar.
Chorus.Stereo Spread: Stereo width of the effect: 100% hard-panned, 0% mono, negative reverses sides, beyond +/-100% widens psychoacoustically.
Chorus.Dimension Mode: Dimension-style output processing: LOW neutral, MED classic Dimension buttons 1-3, HIGH button 4 boost; OFF disables it.
Chorus.Depth 2: Dual Chorus: modulation depth of the left chorus, set separately from the right; raise for more detune on the left side.
Chorus.Center Depth: Undocumented: modulation depth of the centre voice in multi-voice types such as the Tri-Chorus.
Chorus.Depth 3: Dual Chorus: modulation depth of the right chorus, set separately from the left; raise for more detune on the right side.
Chorus.Tempo 2: Undocumented: likely locks LFO2 Rate to a note value of the preset tempo; NONE would leave the manual rate.
Chorus.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Chorus.Delay Range: How far each voice's delay sweeps, 1-40 ms: short gives a subtle shimmer, long a deeper, more obvious detune that suits slow rates.
Chorus.Low: Bass tone of the chorus block's modulated sound, 0-10: lower to keep the low end tight and clear of wobble, raise for a warmer, fuller chorus.
Chorus.High: Treble tone of the chorus block's modulated sound, 0-10: lower for a darker, vintage chorus, raise for a brighter, more present shimmer.

Flanger.Type: Selects the flanger model (analog, thru-zero, classic pedals and racks) and sets the other flanger parameters to suit it.
Flanger.Rate: Speed of the LFO that sweeps the delay; low rate with high depth gives slow jet sweeps, raise rate for vibrato-like effects.
Flanger.Tempo: Locks Rate to a note value of the preset tempo (1/4 at 120 BPM = 2 Hz); set NONE to use the Rate knob instead.
Flanger.Depth: Range of the LFO sweep; at minimum only Manual sets the delay, at maximum the LFO alone controls it.
Flanger.Feedback: Regeneration: higher values give intense, singing or metallic resonance; negative values sound hollow and vocal; extremes can ring.
Flanger.Manual: Sets the delay time by hand to sweep the flanger manually; set Depth to 0 to control it fully, disabled at full Depth.
Flanger.Dry Delay: With Thru-Zero engaged, moves the cancellation point from the centre of the sweep toward its edge.
Flanger.Phase: Phase difference between left and right LFOs; 180 for maximum stereo spread, 0 for mono flanging.
Flanger.Type 2: Shape of the modulation waveform; Sine and Triangle are the usual smooth choices, Square/Saw/Random give choppy or stepped motion.
Flanger.High Cut: Filters the LFO waveform to round off sharp edges; lower it to stop clicks from Square/Saw/Random shapes, slower rates need lower values.
Flanger.Auto Depth: Scales Depth with Rate for a consistent sound at any speed; turn OFF for precise control or wild settings.
Flanger.Mix: Wet/dry balance; 50% is a classic blend (each at -6 dB), raise toward 100% for all-wet effects such as vibrato.
Flanger.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Flanger.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Flanger.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE modes silence all output, or only the effect output while the dry passes.
Flanger.Phase Reverse: Inverts the wet output of one or both channels; widens a mono flanger and deepens thru-zero cancellation (use BOTH).
Flanger.Thru-Zero: OFF for normal flanging, AUTO sweeps through the zero point like tape flanging, MANUAL lets the Manual knob sweep through zero.
Flanger.High Cut 2: Gently rolls off highs of the wet signal (6 dB slope); lower it for a darker, smoother flange.
Flanger.Drive: Simulates the soft distortion of an overdriven analog bucket-brigade chip; 0 is pristine clean, raise for grit.
Flanger.Low Cut: Gently rolls off lows of the wet signal (6 dB slope); raise it to thin the flange and keep bass clear.
Flanger.Stereo Spread: Stereo width of the effect: 100% hard-panned, 0% mono, negative reverses sides, beyond +/-100% widens psychoacoustically.
Flanger.Bypass Reset: Restarts the LFO from the chosen phase each time the block is engaged; OFF lets the LFO run freely even while bypassed.
Flanger.High Cut Order: Undocumented: slope of the wet high-cut filter, from a gentle 6 dB/oct to a steep 36 dB/oct.
Flanger.Low Cut Order: Undocumented: slope of the wet low-cut filter, 6 or 12 dB/oct.
Flanger.Bass Focus: Cuts bass in the wet path while compensating the dry path, so lows stay solid; raise for a tighter, flatter low end.
Flanger.VCO Response: Curve of the sweep to match different flanger designs; LINEAR is a true linear sweep, EXPONENTIAL can sound more musical.
Flanger.Min Time: Shortest delay of the sweep; shorter times give a higher-pitched resonance; set automatically by Type.
Flanger.Max Time: Longest delay of the sweep; longer times reach lower-pitched notches; set automatically by Type.
Flanger.Quantize: Turns the smooth LFO into a series of flat steps like sample-and-hold; more steps is smoother, OFF disables it.
Flanger.Exponent: For EXPONENTIAL VCO only: 1.0 sweeps notches linearly; higher dwells at short (high-pitched) times, lower dwells at long times.
Flanger.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.

Phaser.Type: Selects the phaser model (MXR, Uni-Vibe, Bi-Phase, Small Stone style, barberpole, etc.) and sets other parameters to suit.
Phaser.Order: Number of phase-shift stages; more stages add notches for a more pronounced effect (MXR 90 is 4, Bi-Phase 6, up to 12).
Phaser.Rate: Speed of the LFO that sweeps the phaser; raise for faster swoosh or vibe throb.
Phaser.Type 2: Shape of the modulation waveform; Sine and Triangle are the usual smooth choices, Square/Saw/Random give choppy or stepped motion.
Phaser.Tempo: Locks Rate to a note value of the preset tempo (1/4 at 120 BPM = 2 Hz); set NONE to use the Rate knob instead.
Phaser.Depth: Mix of LFO versus Manual control; higher gives more dramatic sweeps, 0 leaves the phaser parked at the Manual position.
Phaser.Feedback: Regeneration: how pronounced the peaks and notches are; raise for the classic resonant phaser sound, negative values invert it.
Phaser.Min Frequency: Lowest frequency of the sweep range; set automatically by Type, lower it to move the notches down.
Phaser.Max Frequency: Highest frequency of the sweep range; set automatically by Type, raise it to sweep brighter.
Phaser.LFO Phase: Phase of the right LFO versus the left; 0 for mono (before the amp), 180 gives Bi-Phase style stereo phasing.
Phaser.Bias: Bias point of the virtual voltage-controlled resistor; 0 is optimal, negative values push it into cutoff.
Phaser.Mix: Wet/dry balance; real phasers sit near 50%, a higher mix can sound better with feedback, 100% gives Uni-Vibe vibrato.
Phaser.Level: Output level in dB; raise to compensate for the volume loss the phaser's notches cause, especially with drive.
Phaser.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Phaser.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE modes silence all output, or only the effect output while the dry passes.
Phaser.Phaser Mode: Undocumented: selects the core algorithm, normal phaser, Uni-Vibe style vibe, or barberpole (endless sweep).
Phaser.Feedback Point: Where feedback re-enters the stage chain: 0 is before the first stage, 1 the first stage and so on; changes the feedback character.
Phaser.Tone: Simple tone control on the wet signal only; turn up for brighter, down for darker phasing.
Phaser.Sweep Direction: Barberpole type only: whether the endless sweep rises (UP) or falls (DOWN).
Phaser.Filter Q: Barberpole type only: with Feedback, sets the intensity of the effect; raise for a stronger sweep.
Phaser.Reset on Bypass: Restarts the LFO from the chosen phase each time the block is engaged; OFF lets the LFO run freely even while bypassed.
Phaser.Quantize: Turns the smooth LFO into a series of flat steps like sample-and-hold; more steps is smoother, OFF disables it.
Phaser.Type 3: VCR type: LINEAR maps LFO straight to frequency, EXPONENTIAL is more musical, JFET suits pedals, PHOTOCELL mimics a Uni-Vibe's lamp and LDR.
Phaser.Exponent: For EXPONENTIAL VCR only: 1.0 sweeps evenly; higher dwells at high frequencies, lower dwells at low frequencies.
Phaser.Shape: Astable Beta: contour of the LFO when its shape is Astable; low settings are close to Triangle, high settings a half-lazy Square.
Phaser.High Cut: Filters the LFO waveform to round off sharp edges; lower it to stop clicks from Square/Saw/Random shapes, slower rates need lower values.
Phaser.Attack: PHOTOCELL VCR only: photocell attack time; typical about 5 ms, longer smooths the start of each sweep.
Phaser.Release: PHOTOCELL VCR only: photocell release time; typical about 35 ms, shorter gives a lumpier response.
Phaser.Manual: Sets the phaser position by hand from lowest to highest point; controls it fully at Depth 0, no effect at full Depth.
Phaser.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Phaser.Low Cut: High-pass filter on the wet path only; raise to thin the phased signal and keep the lows clean.
Phaser.High Cut 2: Low-pass filter on the wet path only; lower to darken the phased signal.
Phaser.Mode: LFO mode: UNIVIBE makes LFO depth roughly proportional to Rate like a real Uni-Vibe; NORMAL keeps it constant for deep slow sweeps.

Rotary.Rate: Spin speed of drum and horn; slow for chorale, fast for tremolo; 0 parks the rotor.
Rotary.Low Depth: Modulation depth of the drum (bass rotor); raise for a more pronounced throb.
Rotary.Hi Depth: Modulation depth of the horn; reduce fully to simulate a drum-only cabinet.
Rotary.High Level: Output level of the horn relative to the drum; raise for more shimmer, lower for a darker sound.
Rotary.Tempo: Locks Rate to a note value of the preset tempo (1/4 at 120 BPM = 2 Hz); set NONE to use the Rate knob instead.
Rotary.Mix: Wet/dry balance; 50% is a classic blend (each at -6 dB), raise toward 100% for all-wet effects such as vibrato.
Rotary.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Rotary.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Rotary.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE modes silence all output, or only the effect output while the dry passes.
Rotary.Rotor Length: Length of the virtual horn; larger values add Doppler shift for a more intense, chorus-like effect.
Rotary.Mic Spacing: Spacing of the virtual mics, setting stereo width; 0 gives a mono mic on the cabinet, raise for a wider image.
Rotary.Low Rate Mult: Speed of the drum relative to the horn; below 1 makes the drum spin slower, as on a real rotary.
Rotary.Low Time Constant: How long the drum takes to spin up or down when Rate changes; raise for a slower, heavier ramp.
Rotary.Hi Time Constant: How long the horn takes to spin up or down when Rate changes; raise for a slower ramp.
Rotary.Stereo Spread: Stereo width of the effect: 100% hard-panned, 0% mono, negative reverses sides, beyond +/-100% widens psychoacoustically.
Rotary.Drive: Overdrives the virtual rotary amplifier; raise for the grit and grind of the classic cabinet.
Rotary.Mic Distance: Distance of the virtual mics from the cabinet; the effect is subtle.
Rotary.Input Select: Which input feeds the effect: L+R sums stereo to mono (default), or use only LEFT or RIGHT.
Rotary.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.

Pan/Tremolo.Type: Selects tremolo (VCA, bias, optical, neon), harmonic trem or auto-panner; bias and harmonic types may add tube-like distortion.
Pan/Tremolo.LFO Type: Shape of the volume modulation; Sine/Triangle are smooth, Square is choppy on/off, Saw Down mimics Vox percussion trem.
Pan/Tremolo.Rate: Speed of the tremolo or pan cycle; raise for faster pulsing.
Pan/Tremolo.Depth: Intensity of the volume modulation (acts as the mix); raise for a more dramatic, choppier tremolo.
Pan/Tremolo.LFO Duty Cycle: Symmetry of the LFO waveform; changes the peaks from a regular tremolo toward short electronic blobs.
Pan/Tremolo.Tempo: Locks Rate to a note value of the preset tempo (1/4 at 120 BPM = 2 Hz); set NONE to use the Rate knob instead.
Pan/Tremolo.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Pan/Tremolo.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Pan/Tremolo.Bypass Mode: THRU disengages the block like a shunt when bypassed; MUTE silences all output when bypassed.
Pan/Tremolo.LFO Phase: Phase between left and right LFOs; 0 for a true mono tremolo, 180 for perfect panning.
Pan/Tremolo.Width: Panner only: pan width; above 100% creates the illusion of panning beyond the normal stereo image.
Pan/Tremolo.Pan Center: Panner only: shifts the apparent centre of the stereo image left or right.
Pan/Tremolo.Start Phase: Point in the cycle where the tremolo starts when engaged or triggered; adjust to make the first pulse land where wanted.
Pan/Tremolo.Crossover Slope: Harmonic trem only: slope of the crossover splitting the bands; 6 dB/oct is the original circuit, steeper is more intense.
Pan/Tremolo.Crossover Frequency: Harmonic trem only: frequency where the signal splits into the two alternately modulated bands.
Pan/Tremolo.Trigger Threshold: Restarts the tremolo cycle when you start playing above this level, keeping it in time with you; minimum lets it run free.
Pan/Tremolo.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Pan/Tremolo.LFO Shape: Undocumented: likely Astable Beta as in the Phaser, the contour of an Astable LFO shape from Triangle-like to squarer.
Pan/Tremolo.Ducking: Undocumented: likely reduces the tremolo depth as you play louder, so it returns when notes decay.

Formant.Start: Vowel at Control minimum (AAA bat, EEE bait, III beet, OHH boat, OOO boot, EHH bet, AHH bot, AWW bought, UHH but, ERR Bert).
Formant.Mid: Vowel heard with Control at the middle position; pick a different vowel from Start/End for a talk-box morph.
Formant.End: Vowel heard with Control at maximum; the block morphs Start to Mid to End as Control rises.
Formant.Resonance: Resonance of the vowel filters; higher gives a more dramatic, vocal effect but can clip, so keep headroom.
Formant.Control: Morphs between vowels: Start at 0, Mid at 50%, End at 100%; usually driven by a pedal or LFO for talk-box effects.
Formant.Mix: Wet/dry balance; 50% is a classic blend (each at -6 dB), raise toward 100% for all-wet effects such as vibrato.
Formant.Level: Overall output level of the block in dB; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Formant.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Formant.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE modes silence all output, or only the effect output while the dry passes.
Formant.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.

Wah.Type: Selects the wah model (Cry Baby, Vox V846/V845, Clyde McCoy, Colorsound, Morley, Parapedal, Fractal custom); level matches the pedal.
Wah.Frequency Min: Filter frequency at heel-down (Control minimum); lower for deeper, darker heel tones.
Wah.Frequency Max: Filter frequency at toe-down (Control maximum); lower it so a high-gain wah cuts without shrillness.
Wah.Resonance Q: Resonance of the wah filter; higher is more pronounced and vocal, lower is subtler.
Wah.Q Tracking: How much resonance drops as the pedal moves toward toe; raise for less peaky, harsh toe-down tones.
Wah.Control: Wah pedal position (sweep); usually assigned to an expression pedal, or set fixed for a parked, cocked-wah tone.
Wah.Level: Output level in dB; a wah boosts its centre frequency, so lower this if engaging it gets too loud.
Wah.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
