Wah.Bypass Mode: THRU disengages the block like a shunt when bypassed; MUTE silences all output when bypassed.
Wah.Fat: Mixes dry signal back in, up to 50/50 at maximum; raise for a fuller, less nasal wah.
Wah.Drive: Simulates overdriving the wah circuit; raise for subtle grit, interacting with Inductor Bias.
Wah.Control Taper: Pot taper of the sweep; LINEAR is even, LOG nA puts n% of the range at mid travel, changing where the sweep happens.
Wah.Inductor Bias: DC offset of the virtual inductor; with Drive it adds the asymmetric distortion of coveted vintage wahs.
Wah.Low Cut Frequency: High-pass filter like a real wah's coupling capacitor; raise to thin the lows, lower to keep more bass.
Wah.Graphic EQ: Turns the built-in 8-band graphic EQ on or off.
Wah.EQ 160 Hz: Gain of the 160 Hz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 250 Hz: Gain of the 250 Hz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 400 Hz: Gain of the 400 Hz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 640 Hz: Gain of the 640 Hz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 1000 Hz: Gain of the 1 kHz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 1600 Hz: Gain of the 1.6 kHz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 2500 Hz: Gain of the 2.5 kHz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.EQ 4000 Hz: Gain of the 4 kHz band of the built-in 8-band graphic EQ (when Graphic EQ is ON); boost or cut to shape the wah voice.
Wah.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.

Filter.Type: Filter shape: pass, shelf, peaking, notch, tilt EQ, comb, all-pass, or envelope/auto/touch wah; Null only adjusts level, pan and phase.
Filter.Frequency: Centre or cutoff frequency of the filter; also one end of the LFO sweep range.
Filter.Q: Sharpness of the filter; higher is narrower and more resonant; for Shelf 2 types use 0.5-0.707 for classic console curves.
Filter.Gain: Boost or cut at the frequency for shelf, peaking and tilt types; positive boosts, negative cuts; no effect on notch.
Filter.Level: Output level in dB; with the Null type this makes a simple clean boost.
Filter.Balance: Left/right output balance; moving one way makes the opposite channel quieter, affecting wet and dry.
Filter.Bypass Mode: THRU disengages the block like a shunt; MUTE FX OUT mutes the filtered output while leaving the dry signal.
Filter.Order: Filter slope: 2nd is 12 dB/oct, 4th is 24 dB/oct and steeper, more extreme or squelchy.
Filter.Left Pan: Pan position of the left output; use with Right Pan to narrow, widen or convert stereo to mono.
Filter.Right Pan: Pan position of the right output; use with Left Pan to narrow, widen or convert stereo to mono.
Filter.Phase Invert: Inverts the phase of the left, right or both outputs.
Filter.Low Cut: Extra first-order high-pass; raise to remove bass.
Filter.High Cut: Extra first-order low-pass; lower to remove treble and darken.
Filter.Delay Time: Comb types only: higher values space the comb notches more closely, lower spreads them out.
Filter.Depth: Comb types only: intensity of the comb; higher gives deeper notches and peaks.
Filter.Enable: Turns the built-in LFO on to sweep the filter frequency for auto-filter effects; OFF keeps it static.
Filter.Type 2: Shape of the modulation waveform; Sine and Triangle are the usual smooth choices, Square/Saw/Random give choppy or stepped motion.
Filter.Rate: Speed of the built-in LFO that sweeps the filter frequency.
Filter.Duty: Symmetry of the LFO waveform; 50% is symmetric.
Filter.Mod Frequency: Other end of the LFO sweep range, opposite the main Frequency.
Filter.Quantize: Turns the smooth LFO into a series of flat steps like sample-and-hold; more steps is smoother, OFF disables it.
Filter.Order 2: All-pass type only: number of phase-rotation stages (1-12); more stages give progressively more phase rotation.
Filter.Scene Ignore: ON takes this channel outside the scene system so scene changes never alter its channel or bypass; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Filter.Mode: Envelope/auto/touch wah filter output: LOWPASS, BANDPASS or HIGHPASS; MIX blends the bandpass with the dry signal.
Filter.Resonance: Undocumented: resonance of the envelope/auto/touch wah filter; raise for a sharper, more vocal peak.
Filter.Start Frequency: Envelope types: filter frequency at rest; set it above Stop Frequency to sweep downward.
Filter.Stop Frequency: Envelope types: frequency the filter reaches at full envelope; set below Start to sweep down.
Filter.Sensitivity: Envelope types: detector sensitivity; raise so lighter playing opens the filter further, match to guitar and dynamics.
Filter.Attack Time: Envelope types: how fast the filter opens when you pick; defaults match the original Mu-Tron, longer is slower.
Filter.Release Time: Envelope types: how fast the filter closes after a note; longer gives a slower fall back.
Filter.Sweep Shape: Envelope types: detector-to-frequency mapping; 0 is linear, higher values are more nonlinear and quacky.
Filter.Detector Source: Envelope types: what drives the detector, the block input or a hardware input (e.g. guitar input after an amp).
Filter.Emphasis: Envelope types: emphasises highs into the detector to even out the response on higher notes.
Filter.Tempo: Locks the filter LFO rate to a note value of the preset tempo; NONE uses the Rate knob.
Filter.Mix: Wet/dry balance; 50% is a classic blend (each at -6 dB), raise toward 100% for all-wet effects such as vibrato.

Pitch.Type: Selects the shifter algorithm: detune for chorus/doubling, chromatic or diatonic harmony, whammy, octave divider, crystals, arpeggiator, custom or capo.
Pitch.Mode: Classic Whammy shift range: up or down one or two octaves, or both directions; pick the interval the pedal sweep should reach.
Pitch.Master Pitch: Scales the Shift amounts of all voices (not detune); lower toward 0 to narrow the intervals, negative values invert them.
Pitch.Control: Whammy position, usually on a pedal via a modifier; 0% is no shift, raise toward 100% to bend fully to the set interval.
Pitch.Harmony 1: Sets the scale degree voice 1 sounds in diatonic types (3 = a third, 5 = a fifth, 1 = unison); negative values harmonise below.
Pitch.Harmony 2: Sets the scale degree voice 2 sounds in diatonic types (3 = a third, 5 = a fifth, 1 = unison); negative values harmonise below.
Pitch.Harmony 3: Sets the scale degree voice 3 sounds in diatonic types (3 = a third, 5 = a fifth, 1 = unison); negative values harmonise below.
Pitch.Harmony 4: Sets the scale degree voice 4 sounds in diatonic types (3 = a third, 5 = a fifth, 1 = unison); negative values harmonise below.
Pitch.Key: Sets the key the intelligent (diatonic/arpeggiator) harmony works in; match it to the song's key or harmonies will clash.
Pitch.Scale: Sets the scale or mode that harmony notes are drawn from; match the song (e.g. Ionian for major, Aeolian for minor).
Pitch.Pitch Quantize: Undocumented: STEPPED snaps harmony pitch to exact notes (Fractal wiki's auto-tune tip), SMOOTH lets it follow bends and vibrato.
Pitch.Detune 1: Detunes voice 1 by up to 50 cents; about 5-10 gives doubling/chorus, larger values a wider, more out-of-tune spread.
Pitch.Detune 2: Detunes voice 2 by up to 50 cents; about 5-10 gives doubling/chorus, larger values a wider, more out-of-tune spread.
Pitch.Detune 3: Detunes voice 3 by up to 50 cents; about 5-10 gives doubling/chorus, larger values a wider, more out-of-tune spread.
Pitch.Detune 4: Detunes voice 4 by up to 50 cents; about 5-10 gives doubling/chorus, larger values a wider, more out-of-tune spread.
Pitch.Shift 1: Shifts voice 1 up or down by semitones (up to 24); 12 is an octave, 7 a fifth, negative values shift down.
Pitch.Shift 2: Shifts voice 2 up or down by semitones (up to 24); 12 is an octave, 7 a fifth, negative values shift down.
Pitch.Shift 3: Shifts voice 3 up or down by semitones (up to 24); 12 is an octave, 7 a fifth, negative values shift down.
Pitch.Shift 4: Shifts voice 4 up or down by semitones (up to 24); 12 is an octave, 7 a fifth, negative values shift down.
Pitch.Level 1: Sets the volume of voice 1; raise to bring that shifted voice forward, 0% mutes it.
Pitch.Level 2: Sets the volume of voice 2; raise to bring that shifted voice forward, 0% mutes it.
Pitch.Level 3: Sets the volume of voice 3; raise to bring that shifted voice forward, 0% mutes it.
Pitch.Level 4: Sets the volume of voice 4; raise to bring that shifted voice forward, 0% mutes it.
Pitch.Pan 1: Sets the stereo position of voice 1; negative is left, positive right.
Pitch.Pan 2: Sets the stereo position of voice 2; negative is left, positive right.
Pitch.Pan 3: Sets the stereo position of voice 3; negative is left, positive right.
Pitch.Pan 4: Sets the stereo position of voice 4; negative is left, positive right.
Pitch.Delay 1: Sets the delay time of voice 1 (0-2000 ms); short for thickening, longer for echoes of the harmony.
Pitch.Delay 2: Sets the delay time of voice 2 (0-2000 ms); short for thickening, longer for echoes of the harmony.
Pitch.Delay 3: Sets the delay time of voice 3 (0-2000 ms); short for thickening, longer for echoes of the harmony.
Pitch.Delay 4: Sets the delay time of voice 4 (0-2000 ms); short for thickening, longer for echoes of the harmony.
Pitch.Feedback 1: Sets feedback (repeats) for voice 1's delay; raise for more echoes, or spiralling pitch where the shift is inside the loop.
Pitch.Feedback 2: Sets feedback (repeats) for voice 2's delay; raise for more echoes, or spiralling pitch where the shift is inside the loop.
Pitch.Feedback 3: Sets feedback (repeats) for voice 3's delay; raise for more echoes, or spiralling pitch where the shift is inside the loop.
Pitch.Feedback 4: Sets feedback (repeats) for voice 4's delay; raise for more echoes, or spiralling pitch where the shift is inside the loop.
Pitch.Pitch Tracking: NOTES is optimised for single-note playing; CHORDS is more stable on chords (best for capo use) but can add latency.
Pitch.Tracking Adjust: Fine-tunes the shifter's splice length; lower cuts latency but can add artifacts, about 5 is a good compromise.
Pitch.Mix: Sets the wet/dry balance; raise toward 100% for more effect and less dry signal, 50% puts both at -6 dB.
Pitch.Level: Sets the block's overall output level in dB; raise to make the block louder, lower to make it quieter.
Pitch.Balance: Shifts the block's output left or right (wet and dry); the opposite side gets quieter, keep at 0 for centred.
Pitch.Bypass Mode: Sets what bypass does: THRU passes dry untouched, MUTE FX OUT/MUTE OUT silence effect/all, MUTE FX IN/MUTE IN let tails ring out.
Pitch.Input Gain: Sets how much signal feeds the shifter (like an aux send) without changing the dry; lower it to reduce the effect.
Pitch.Crossfade Time: Sets how much Crystal Echoes slices overlap (crossfade); raise for a smoother, softer crystal sound, lower for choppier grains.
Pitch.Crossfade Type: Undocumented: the curve used to crossfade pitch-shifter splices, LINEAR or a smoother HANN window.
Pitch.Time 1: Crystal Echoes splice (granule) length for voice 1 in ms; short times sound grainy and glitchy, longer times smoother.
Pitch.Time 2: Crystal Echoes splice (granule) length for voice 2 in ms; short times sound grainy and glitchy, longer times smoother.
Pitch.Tempo 1: Sets voice 1's delay time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Delay 1.
Pitch.Tempo 2: Sets voice 2's delay time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Delay 2.
Pitch.Tempo 3: Sets voice 3's delay time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Delay 3.
Pitch.Tempo 4: Sets voice 4's delay time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Delay 4.
Pitch.Tempo 1 2: Sets Crystal Echoes splice 1 time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Time 1.
Pitch.Tempo 2 2: Sets Crystal Echoes splice 2 time in rhythmic relation to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual Time 2.
Pitch.Feedback Type: Crystal feedback routing: DUAL feeds each voice back to itself, BOTH mixes voices into both delays, PING-PONG crosses them over.
Pitch.Direction: Plays the shifter's audio granules FORWARD or REVERSE; reverse gives a backwards, shimmering crystal texture.
Pitch.High Cut: Gently rolls off highs (6 dB/oct) on the wet signal only; lower it (around 2-5 kHz) to darken thin, digital-sounding shifted voices.
Pitch.Glide Time: Sets how quickly the harmony slides from one pitch to the next as you play new notes; raise for a slower portamento.
Pitch.Master Delay: Scales the delay times of all voices together; lower to tighten, raise to lengthen every voice's delay.
Pitch.Master Feedback: Scales the feedback of all voice delay lines together; raise for more repeats, lower for fewer.
Pitch.Master Pan: Scales all voice pans as a width control; lower toward 0 to narrow to mono, negative values swap left and right.
Pitch.Master Level: Scales the output level of all voices together; lower to make the shifted voices quieter overall.
Pitch.# of Notes: Sets how many notes (4-8) the custom diatonic scale has when Scale is set to CUSTOM.
Pitch.Scale 1: Custom Shifter: selects which global custom scale (set up in Global Settings) voice 1 uses to choose its harmony note.
Pitch.Scale 2: Custom Shifter: selects which global custom scale (set up in Global Settings) voice 2 uses to choose its harmony note.
Pitch.Steps: Sets the number of steps in the arpeggiator sequence; more steps make a longer melodic pattern.
Pitch.Repeats: Sets how many times the arpeggiator sequence repeats once triggered; raise for longer runs.
Pitch.Run: Starts the arpeggiator sequence when ON; OFF stops it and resets to the first step.
Pitch.Tempo: Sets the duration of each arpeggiator step as a rhythmic value of the preset tempo; shorter values give faster patterns.
Pitch.Step 1 Shift: Arpeggiator step 1: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 2 Shift: Arpeggiator step 2: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 3 Shift: Arpeggiator step 3: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 4 Shift: Arpeggiator step 4: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 5 Shift: Arpeggiator step 5: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 6 Shift: Arpeggiator step 6: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 7 Shift: Arpeggiator step 7: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 8 Shift: Arpeggiator step 8: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 9 Shift: Arpeggiator step 9: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 10 Shift: Arpeggiator step 10: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 11 Shift: Arpeggiator step 11: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 12 Shift: Arpeggiator step 12: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 13 Shift: Arpeggiator step 13: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 14 Shift: Arpeggiator step 14: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 15 Shift: Arpeggiator step 15: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Step 16 Shift: Arpeggiator step 16: scale degrees the note is shifted above or below the note played (0 = unison, 2 = third, 4 = fifth).
Pitch.Amplitude Shape: Sets how the arpeggiator's volume changes across the sequence (constant, rising, falling, up/down, sine).
Pitch.Amplitude Alpha: Sets how strongly the Amplitude Shape is applied; 0% has no effect, 100% is extreme.
Pitch.Pan Shape: Sets how the arpeggiator's pan position moves across the sequence (constant, rising, falling, up/down, sine).
Pitch.Pan Alpha: Sets how strongly the Pan Shape is applied; 0% has no effect, 100% is extreme.
Pitch.Delay Time 1: Sets the delay of detune voice 1 (0-250 ms); about 7 ms adds stereo width to doubling, longer times become slapback.
Pitch.Delay Time 2: Sets the delay of detune voice 2 (0-250 ms); about 7 ms adds stereo width to doubling, longer times become slapback.
Pitch.Detector Source: Chooses where pitch is detected: BLOCK IN follows the block input (incl. tails), an INPUT tracks your clean guitar for best accuracy.
Pitch.Input Mode: MONO sums the input before shifting; STEREO sends left and right to separate voices for stereo shifting.
Pitch.Learn: While ON, the Key follows whatever single note you play; turn OFF again for normal harmonizing.
Pitch.Low Cut: Gently rolls off lows (6 dB/oct) on the wet signal only; raise it to thin out muddy shifted voices, especially octaves down.
Pitch.Feedback Mode: Quad Detune feedback: INDIVIDUAL per voice, or SUMMED to every voice, which can run away; lower Feedback before switching.
Pitch.LFO Rate: Speed of the LFO modulating the detune; raise for faster chorus/vibrato movement.
Pitch.LFO Tempo: Syncs the detune LFO rate to the preset tempo; set NONE to use the manual LFO Rate.
Pitch.LFO Depth: Amount of LFO pitch modulation on the detune; raise for a deeper chorus or vibrato, 0 for static detune.
Pitch.Temperament: EQUAL tunes harmonies to fretted notes; JUST uses pure harmonic ratios for sweeter harmonies, especially into distortion.
Pitch.Diffusion: Crystal Echoes: low keeps crystals discrete, higher smears transients for a softer sound.
Pitch.Diffusion Time: Undocumented: the time (size) of the crystal diffuser smearing, longer for a more washed-out texture.
Pitch.Scene Ignore: When ON this channel ignores scene changes for bypass and channel, so only manual switching controls it; leave OFF for normal scenes.
Pitch.Kill Dry: When ON the dry signal is muted, for parallel routing; set the wet level with Mix and leave Level at 0 dB.
Pitch.Trigger Threshold: Undocumented: input level a note must exceed to trigger the shifter or arpeggiator; lower it to trigger on softer picking.

Synth.Type: Oscillator waveform for voice 1: sine is pure, square/saw are buzzy and bright, noise for effects; OFF silences it and saves CPU.
Synth.Frequency: Sets the voice 1 oscillator pitch in Hz when Track is OFF or ENV ONLY (440 = A); raise for a higher note.
Synth.Track: Voice 1 tracking: OFF is manual pitch and level, ENV ONLY follows your dynamics, PITCH+ENV follows notes and dynamics.
Synth.Shift: Shifts the voice 1 oscillator up or down in semitones; 12 is an octave up, -12 an octave down.
Synth.Tune: Detunes the voice 1 oscillator by up to 50 cents; slight offsets between voices give a fatter synth.
Synth.Duty Cycle: For triangle or square waves, sets voice 1 symmetry or pulse width; move away from 50% for a thinner, nasal tone.
Synth.Voice 1 Level: Sets the output level of synth voice 1; raise to bring it forward in the mix, 0% mutes it.
Synth.Voice 1 Pan: Sets the stereo position of synth voice 1; negative is left, positive right.
Synth.Attack: Attack time of the voice 1 input envelope follower; raise for slower, swelling note onsets, lower for snappy attacks.
Synth.Filter Frequency: Cutoff of the low-pass filter after the voice 1 oscillator; lower it to darken and soften, raise for a brighter tone.
Synth.Filter Q: Resonance of the voice 1 low-pass filter; raise for a peaky emphasis at the cutoff, lower for a smooth roll-off.
Synth.Type 2: Oscillator waveform for voice 2: sine is pure, square/saw are buzzy and bright, noise for effects; OFF silences it and saves CPU.
Synth.Frequency 2: Sets the voice 2 oscillator pitch in Hz when Track is OFF or ENV ONLY (440 = A); raise for a higher note.
Synth.Track 2: Voice 2 tracking: OFF is manual pitch and level, ENV ONLY follows your dynamics, PITCH+ENV follows notes and dynamics.
Synth.Shift 2: Shifts the voice 2 oscillator up or down in semitones; 12 is an octave up, -12 an octave down.
Synth.Tune 2: Detunes the voice 2 oscillator by up to 50 cents; slight offsets between voices give a fatter synth.
Synth.Duty Cycle 2: For triangle or square waves, sets voice 2 symmetry or pulse width; move away from 50% for a thinner, nasal tone.
Synth.Voice 2 Level: Sets the output level of synth voice 2; raise to bring it forward in the mix, 0% mutes it.
Synth.Voice 2 Pan: Sets the stereo position of synth voice 2; negative is left, positive right.
Synth.Attack 2: Attack time of the voice 2 input envelope follower; raise for slower, swelling note onsets, lower for snappy attacks.
Synth.Filter Frequency 2: Cutoff of the low-pass filter after the voice 2 oscillator; lower it to darken and soften, raise for a brighter tone.
Synth.Filter Q 2: Resonance of the voice 2 low-pass filter; raise for a peaky emphasis at the cutoff, lower for a smooth roll-off.
Synth.Mix: Sets the wet/dry balance; raise toward 100% for more effect and less dry signal, 50% puts both at -6 dB.
Synth.Level: Sets the block's overall output level in dB; raise to make the block louder, lower to make it quieter.
Synth.Balance: Shifts the block's output left or right (wet and dry); the opposite side gets quieter, keep at 0 for centred.
Synth.Bypass Mode: Sets what bypass does: THRU passes dry untouched, MUTE FX OUT silences only the effect, MUTE OUT silences the whole block output.
Synth.Type 3: Oscillator waveform for voice 3: sine is pure, square/saw are buzzy and bright, noise for effects; OFF silences it and saves CPU.
Synth.Frequency 3: Sets the voice 3 oscillator pitch in Hz when Track is OFF or ENV ONLY (440 = A); raise for a higher note.
Synth.Track 3: Voice 3 tracking: OFF is manual pitch and level, ENV ONLY follows your dynamics, PITCH+ENV follows notes and dynamics.
Synth.Shift 3: Shifts the voice 3 oscillator up or down in semitones; 12 is an octave up, -12 an octave down.
Synth.Tune 3: Detunes the voice 3 oscillator by up to 50 cents; slight offsets between voices give a fatter synth.
Synth.Duty Cycle 3: For triangle or square waves, sets voice 3 symmetry or pulse width; move away from 50% for a thinner, nasal tone.
Synth.Voice 3 Level: Sets the output level of synth voice 3; raise to bring it forward in the mix, 0% mutes it.
Synth.Voice 3 Pan: Sets the stereo position of synth voice 3; negative is left, positive right.
Synth.Attack 3: Attack time of the voice 3 input envelope follower; raise for slower, swelling note onsets, lower for snappy attacks.
Synth.Filter Frequency 3: Cutoff of the low-pass filter after the voice 3 oscillator; lower it to darken and soften, raise for a brighter tone.
Synth.Filter Q 3: Resonance of the voice 3 low-pass filter; raise for a peaky emphasis at the cutoff, lower for a smooth roll-off.
Synth.Scene Ignore: When ON this channel ignores scene changes for bypass and channel, so only manual switching controls it; leave OFF for normal scenes.
Synth.Tracking Mode: Sets the pitch tracking range: BASS shifts tracking down an octave (to about F#0) for bass; use GUITAR for guitar.

Ring Modulator.Frequency: Sets the modulating oscillator frequency; low values give tremolo-like wobble, higher values clangorous, bell-like inharmonic tones.
Ring Modulator.Frequency Multiplier: Scales the oscillator frequency 0.25-4x; with Pitch Tracking ON, 0.5 gives a clean octave down, other ratios get wilder.
Ring Modulator.Pitch Tracking: When ON the oscillator follows the pitch of notes played, giving musically predictable tones across the neck.
Ring Modulator.High Cut Frequency: Filters highs from the ring modulator sound; lower it to tame harsh, fizzy sidebands.
Ring Modulator.Mix: Sets the wet/dry balance; raise toward 100% for more effect and less dry signal, 50% puts both at -6 dB.
Ring Modulator.Level: Sets the block's overall output level in dB; raise to make the block louder, lower to make it quieter.
Ring Modulator.Balance: Shifts the block's output left or right (wet and dry); the opposite side gets quieter, keep at 0 for centred.
Ring Modulator.Bypass Mode: Sets what bypass does: THRU passes dry untouched, MUTE FX OUT silences only the effect, MUTE OUT silences the whole block output.
Ring Modulator.Type: CLASSIC gives both sum and difference tones; SSB UPPER or SSB LOWER keeps only the upper or lower sideband.
Ring Modulator.Scene Ignore: When ON this channel ignores scene changes for bypass and channel, so only manual switching controls it; leave OFF for normal scenes.
Ring Modulator.Tracking Mode: Sets the pitch tracking range: BASS shifts tracking down an octave (to about F#0) for bass; use GUITAR for guitar.

Resonator.Mode: MANUAL sets the four resonator frequencies individually; CHORDAL sets them automatically from a chord type and root.
Resonator.Chord Type: In CHORDAL mode, selects the chord the four resonators are tuned to (major, minor, 7ths, diminished, augmented).
Resonator.Input Gain: Sets how much signal feeds the resonators (like an aux send) without changing the dry; lower it to reduce the effect.
Resonator.Frequency: In CHORDAL mode, sets the chord root frequency; raise to pitch the whole resonant chord higher.
Resonator.Master Frequency: In MANUAL mode, scales all four resonator frequencies together; modulate it for a high flanger-like sweep.
Resonator.Master Level: Scales the output levels of all four resonators; lower to make the resonance quieter overall.
Resonator.Master Pan: Scales all four resonator pans as a width control; negative values reverse the stereo image.
Resonator.Master Feedback: Scales the feedback (resonance) of all four resonators; raise for longer, more metallic ringing.
Resonator.Master Q: Scales the Q of all four bandpass filters; raise for narrower, more focused tones.
Resonator.Frequency 2: Manual mode: resonant frequency of resonator 1 and its bandpass filter (100-10,000 Hz); raise to pitch that resonance higher.
Resonator.Frequency 3: Manual mode: resonant frequency of resonator 2 and its bandpass filter (100-10,000 Hz); raise to pitch that resonance higher.
Resonator.Frequency 4: Manual mode: resonant frequency of resonator 3 and its bandpass filter (100-10,000 Hz); raise to pitch that resonance higher.
Resonator.Frequency 5: Manual mode: resonant frequency of resonator 4 and its bandpass filter (100-10,000 Hz); raise to pitch that resonance higher.
Resonator.Feedback: Resonance of resonator 1, set by its comb-filter feedback; raise for longer, ringing metallic tones, negative values invert it.
Resonator.Feedback 2: Resonance of resonator 2, set by its comb-filter feedback; raise for longer, ringing metallic tones, negative values invert it.
Resonator.Feedback 3: Resonance of resonator 3, set by its comb-filter feedback; raise for longer, ringing metallic tones, negative values invert it.
Resonator.Feedback 4: Resonance of resonator 4, set by its comb-filter feedback; raise for longer, ringing metallic tones, negative values invert it.
Resonator.Fltr Location: Places resonator 1's bandpass filter PRE (before) or POST (after) its comb resonator.
Resonator.Fltr Location 2: Places resonator 2's bandpass filter PRE (before) or POST (after) its comb resonator.
Resonator.Fltr Location 3: Places resonator 3's bandpass filter PRE (before) or POST (after) its comb resonator.
Resonator.Fltr Location 4: Places resonator 4's bandpass filter PRE (before) or POST (after) its comb resonator.
Resonator.Q: Q of resonator 1's bandpass filter; raise for a narrower, more focused band, lower for a broader one.
Resonator.Q 2: Q of resonator 2's bandpass filter; raise for a narrower, more focused band, lower for a broader one.
Resonator.Q 3: Q of resonator 3's bandpass filter; raise for a narrower, more focused band, lower for a broader one.
Resonator.Q 4: Q of resonator 4's bandpass filter; raise for a narrower, more focused band, lower for a broader one.
Resonator.Level: Output level of resonator 1; raise to bring its note forward, 0% mutes it.
Resonator.Level 2: Output level of resonator 2; raise to bring its note forward, 0% mutes it.
Resonator.Level 3: Output level of resonator 3; raise to bring its note forward, 0% mutes it.
Resonator.Level 4: Output level of resonator 4; raise to bring its note forward, 0% mutes it.
Resonator.Pan: Stereo position of resonator 1; negative is left, positive right.
Resonator.Pan 2: Stereo position of resonator 2; negative is left, positive right.
Resonator.Pan 3: Stereo position of resonator 3; negative is left, positive right.
Resonator.Pan 4: Stereo position of resonator 4; negative is left, positive right.
Resonator.Mix: Sets the wet/dry balance; raise toward 100% for more effect and less dry signal, 50% puts both at -6 dB.
Resonator.Level 5: Sets the block's overall output level in dB; raise to make the block louder, lower to make it quieter.
Resonator.Balance: Shifts the block's output left or right (wet and dry); the opposite side gets quieter, keep at 0 for centred.
Resonator.Bypass Mode: Sets what bypass does: THRU passes dry untouched, MUTE FX OUT silences only the effect, MUTE OUT silences the whole block output.
Resonator.Input Mode: MONO feeds both inputs summed to all four resonators; STEREO feeds left to resonators 1-2 and right to 3-4.

Reverb.Bypass Mode: What bypass does: THRU removes the block entirely, MUTE IN/MUTE FX IN let reverb tails spill over, MUTE/MUTE OUT/MUTE FX OUT cut tails at once.
Reverb.Scene Ignore: When ON this channel ignores scene changes, so its bypass and channel change only by manual control; leave OFF for normal scene switching.
Reverb.Kill Dry: Removes the dry signal so only reverb leaves the block; turn on when the reverb sits on a parallel row and set the wet amount with Mix.
Reverb.Type: Selects the reverb model (room, hall, plate, spring, echo, shimmer and so on), which loads that space's character; choose by the space you want heard.
Reverb.High Freq Decay Time: High-band decay relative to Time: lower makes highs die faster for a darker, softer tail (curtains); 1.0 means no high-frequency absorption.
Reverb.Wall Diffusion: How fast the tail's density builds: lower keeps discrete echoes audible longer, higher builds density quickly for a washier sound.
Reverb.Size: Size of the space or spring: larger gives longer gaps, more delay before onset, grainier and darker; small is smoother but very small turns metallic.
Reverb.Reverbdelay: Undocumented: an internal delay before the reverb tail, separate from Pre-Delay; more would push the tail later.
Reverb.Early Level: Level of the early reflections (no effect on Springs); raise it and lower Late Level for an amp-in-the-room ambience.
Reverb.Late Level: Level of the reverb tail; lower it with Early Level up for room ambience, raise it for a fuller, longer wash.
Reverb.Depth: Modulation depth in the reverb tail for a chorus-like, lusher sound; set to zero to defeat for a static, natural reverb.
Reverb.Rate: Speed of the reverb tail's modulation; raise for faster shimmer, lower for slow, subtle movement.
Reverb.Input Gain: Amount of signal fed into the reverb without changing the dry level; lower for less reverb while keeping Mix and the dry volume fixed.
Reverb.Echo Density: Density of the tail: higher is smoother (good for percussive playing), lower lets individual repeats be heard; higher also costs CPU.
Reverb.Input Diffusion: Amount of the input diffuser that smears transients before the reverb; raise for a smoother onset, lower for more defined attacks.
Reverb.Input Diff Time: Time of the input diffuser that smears transients; adjust with Input Diffusion to change how smooth the reverb onset sounds.
Reverb.Number of Springs: Number of springs in a Spring type; more springs give a denser reverb, fewer a sparser, more twangy one.
Reverb.Spring Tone: Tonal colour of the virtual springs; lower values are darker, higher values brighter.
Reverb.Mic Spacing: Stereo width of the early reflections by simulating mic separation in the space; raise for wider, lower for narrower.
Reverb.Freq 1: Centre frequency of the low-mid peaking EQ on the reverb only (20 Hz-2 kHz); pick the range Gain 1 boosts or cuts.
Reverb.Freq 2: Centre frequency of the high-mid peaking EQ on the reverb only (100 Hz-10 kHz); pick the range Gain 2 boosts or cuts.
Reverb.Q 1: Width of the low-mid reverb EQ band: higher Q is narrower and more surgical, lower Q broader.
Reverb.Q 2: Width of the high-mid reverb EQ band: higher Q is narrower and more surgical, lower Q broader.
Reverb.Gain 1: Boost or cut at Freq 1 on the reverb only, not the dry; cut to clear muddy lows from the tail, boost to add warmth.
Reverb.Gain 2: Boost or cut at Freq 2 on the reverb only, not the dry; cut to tame harsh tails, boost to add sparkle.
Reverb.Spring Drive: Spring dwell: higher drives the springs harder for a splashier sound; it is level-compensated so it does not change the mix.
Reverb.Low Freq Decay Time: Low-band decay relative to Time (2.0 is twice as long); lower it to reduce low-frequency buildup and mud.
Reverb.Crossover Frequency: Crossover between the low and mid decay bands; sets which frequencies Low Freq Decay Time controls.
Reverb.Spread: Stereo width of the reverb: 100% is full stereo, 0% mono, negative reverses sides, beyond 100% sounds wider than the speakers.
Reverb.Attenuation: Ducker depth: how much the reverb drops while you play above Threshold; 0 dB defeats ducking, raise to keep busy playing clear.
Reverb.Threshold: Ducker trigger level: input above it ducks the reverb by Attenuation; lower it to duck more readily.
Reverb.Release Time: How fast the ducked reverb returns once input falls below Threshold: short snaps back, long swells back gradually.
Reverb.Early Diffusion: Diffusion of the early reflections: higher gives fuzzier, less distinct echoes, lower gives sharp, distinct reflections.
Reverb.Early Diff Time: Scales the delay time of the early-reflection diffusers; adjust to suit the size and character of the simulated space.
Reverb.Early Decay: Decay rate of the early reflections; higher values make them decay faster.
Reverb.Late Input Mix: Feeds early reflections into the tail generator (High quality); raise to blend them into the tail, 0% behaves like Normal quality.
Reverb.Quality: Algorithm quality vs CPU: ECONOMY and NORMAL suit most live guitar, HIGH is smoother and more natural, ULTRA-HIGH richer still at more CPU.
Reverb.Stack/Hold: Infinite reverb: HOLD mutes the input and freezes the current tail, STACK freezes it while still layering new playing; OFF is normal.
Reverb.Basetype: Undocumented: the internal base algorithm behind the selected Type, set by the model rather than tuned by ear.
Reverb.LFO Phase: Phase of the right side's tail modulation relative to the left; raise toward 180 for wider, more swirling stereo movement.
Reverb.Input Select: Which input feeds the reverb: L+R sums both (default), LEFT or RIGHT uses one side only.
Reverb.Boiiinnng!: Dispersion: the drip and springiness of springs or the laser-like 'pew' of plates; raise to exaggerate it, lower for less (and less CPU).
Reverb.Low Cut Slope: Steepness of the reverb's low cut: 12 dB/OCT removes lows more sharply than 6 dB/OCT and enables Low Q.
Reverb.High Cut Slope: Steepness of the reverb's high cut: 12 dB/OCT darkens more sharply than 6 dB/OCT and enables High Q.
Reverb.Mix 2: Pitch Mix: how much of the built-in pitch shifter is in the reverb, for shimmer; 0% for none, raise for more shimmer.
Reverb.Voice 1 Shift: Pitch shift of shifter voice 1 in semitones (e.g. 12 for an octave-up shimmer); 0 for no shift.
Reverb.Voice 2 Shift: Pitch shift of shifter voice 2 in semitones (e.g. 24 for two octaves up); 0 for no shift.
Reverb.Feedback: Pitch Feedback: regenerates the shifted signal so it climbs further; keep low or zero with MATRIX or FEEDBACK position to avoid instability.
Reverb.Direction: Plays the pitch shifter grains forward or reverse: FORWARD, REVERSE, or FOR/REV and REV/FOR to split voice 1 and voice 2.
Reverb.Splice Time: Length in ms of the audio granules the pitch shifter splices together; adjust to change the shimmer's texture.
Reverb.Position: Where the shifters sit: INPUT before the reverb, MATRIX inside it or FEEDBACK in its loop for more intense shimmer that tracks notes better.
Reverb.Modulation: Undocumented: modulation applied to the reverb's pitch shifter voices; raise for more movement in the shimmer.
Reverb.Voice Balance: Blend between pitch voice 1 and voice 2; move negative for more voice 1, positive for more voice 2.
Reverb.Tempo: Syncs the pre-delay echo time to the preset tempo as a note value; NONE uses the set Pre-Delay time.
Reverb.Feedback 2: Pre-Delay Feedback: repeats the pre-delay for simple echoes before the reverb; raise for more echo repeats, 0% for a single pre-delay.
Reverb.Echo Mix: Pre-Delay Mix: sends pre-delay echoes around the reverb to the output; raise for audible echoes, 100% gives discrete echoes with no reverb.
Reverb.Pitch High Cut: High cut on the pitch-shifted part of the reverb; lower to darken the shimmer, raise to brighten it.
Reverb.Tank Type: Spring tank wiring: PARALLEL (all springs side by side, British/Studio Spring) or SERIES-PARALLEL (Fender-style coupled pairs); set by the model.
Reverb.Tonetype: Undocumented: the spring model's tone-control circuit variant (Fractal notes models have different tone controls), set by the model.
Reverb.Tap: Pre-Delay Tap: OUTPUT keeps the normal initial delay, INPUT removes it for more natural echo-verb sounds when using the pre-delay echoes.
Reverb.Low Q: Resonance of the reverb's low cut filter, only active at 12 dB/OCT slope; raise for a bump at the cutoff.
Reverb.High Q: Resonance of the reverb's high cut filter, only active at 12 dB/OCT slope; raise for a bump at the cutoff.
Reverb.Mix: Wet/dry balance; raising it lowers the dry level, so 50% puts both at -6 dB; set by ear, or use 100% with Kill Dry in parallel.
Reverb.Level: Overall output volume of the whole block, wet and dry together; raise or lower to match the bypassed volume.
Reverb.Balance: Left/right balance of the block's output, wet and dry; moving toward one side makes the opposite channel quieter.
Reverb.Time: Decay time (RT60) of the reverb's mid band, up to 100 s; raise for a longer tail, lower for a tighter one (amp springs run about 2.75-4 s).
Reverb.High Cut: Low-pass filter on the reverb only; lower it to darken the tail so it sits behind the guitar, raise for a brighter reverb.
Reverb.Low Cut: High-pass filter on the reverb only; raise it to remove low-end mud from the tail, lower for a fuller reverb.
Reverb.Pre-Delay: Extra delay before the reverb starts, beyond what Size gives; raise to keep the reverb out of the attack's way, 0 for a natural room.
Reverb.Type families: Room is short and natural, Hall long and natural, Chamber bright and boxy, Plate smooth, Spring a guitar-amp tank, Huge/Cloud/SFX/Echo ambient or special.

Input.Threshold: Level (dB) below which the input noise gate closes; raise it toward 0 to gate more noise, lower it so quiet notes and decays are not cut.
Input.Ratio: How much quieter the signal gets when the gate is closed (output dB = input dB / ratio); 1 does nothing, raise to 3-4 to silence high-gain hiss.
Input.Release: How long (ms) the gate takes to close; longer gives a gradual natural decay, very short clamps tightly but can chatter (Fractal: ~100-200 ms).
Input.Attack: How fast (ms) the gate opens once signal exceeds threshold; keep it short (under ~5-10 ms) so the attack of first notes punches through.
Input.Input1/Instr Impedance: Load the instrument input presents to the pickups: AUTO follows the first active pedal model; lower values (e.g. 22K) darken pickups like vintage fuzz.
Input.Output Level: Level (dB) leaving the input gate into the grid, working even with the gate off; raise to hit a drive or compressor harder, lower to tame hot pickups.
Input.Gate Type: CLASSIC opens and closes like a typical gate; INTELLIGENT and NOISE REDUCER add smart filtering and hum (EMI) reduction for less obvious gating.
Input.Mode: EASY hides the gate's Attack and Release to simplify editing; ADVANCED shows them; it does not change the sound by itself.

Gate/Expander.Threshold: Level (dB) below which expansion or gating starts; raise to remove more noise between notes, lower so soft playing and tails pass.
Gate/Expander.Attack: How fast (ms) the gate opens when level exceeds threshold; keep low so first-note attack punches through, set high for a slow-gear swell.
Gate/Expander.Hold: Time (ms) the gate is held open after the threshold is exceeded (certain types only); longer avoids chopping short gaps between notes.
Gate/Expander.Release: How long (ms) the gate takes to close below threshold; slow for gradual decay of sustained notes, fast for tight djent-style silence between notes.
Gate/Expander.Ratio: Expander types: how much quieter signal below threshold becomes (output dB = input dB / ratio); 1 changes nothing, higher expands harder.
Gate/Expander.Low Cut: High-pass filter (Hz) on the sidechain detector only, not the output tone; raise so low-string thump does not hold the gate open.
Gate/Expander.High Cut: Low-pass filter (Hz) on the sidechain detector only, not the output tone; lower so hiss and pick noise do not trigger the gate.
Gate/Expander.Level: Overall output level (dB) of the block; raise or lower to balance volume after gating.
Gate/Expander.Sidechain Source: Signal the detector listens to: BLOCK L+R is the block's own input (normal); a row or input lets it gate from a cleaner source or duck/de-ess.
Gate/Expander.Balance: Pans the block's stereo output: moving left or right makes the opposite channel quieter (wet and dry); leave at 0 for centred.
Gate/Expander.Bypass Mode: What happens when the block is bypassed: THRU passes the signal untouched like a shunt, MUTE silences it.
Gate/Expander.Type: Classic Expander/Gate act like vintage units (gate is harder), Modern Gate opens with a slower linear-in-dB attack, Modern Expander has improved ballistics.
Gate/Expander.Attenuation: Gate types: how much quieter (dB) the signal is when the gate is closed; -80 dB silences fully, smaller values leave some sound through.
Gate/Expander.Detector Type: How the level is measured: PEAK reacts to transients quickly, RMS is smoother and more average-based.
Gate/Expander.Scene Ignore: Per channel: ON stops scene changes from setting this block's bypass or channel once that channel is selected; leave OFF for normal scene control.
Gate/Expander.Knee Type: Modern Expander only: how sharply expansion starts around the threshold, from HARD (abrupt) to SOFT (gradual and less noticeable).

Drive.Drive Model: Selects the modelled pedal (boost, overdrive, distortion or fuzz type); each recreates a specific circuit and sets its own voicing.
Drive.Drive: Gain of the modelled pedal, like its drive/distortion knob; raise for more saturation, lower (toward 0) to use it as a clean-ish boost.
Drive.Tone: The modelled pedal's own tone knob, working as on the original; raise for brighter, lower for darker.
Drive.Level: Output volume of the pedal (0-10) like its level knob; raise to push the amp harder or boost volume, lower to reduce output.
Drive.Mix: Blend of clean to distorted signal inside the drive stage, before the tone controls; normally 100%, lower for more transparency and attack.
Drive.Bypass Mode: What happens when the block is bypassed: THRU passes the signal untouched like a shunt, MUTE silences it.
Drive.Slew Rate: Simulates early op-amps' limited slew rate: higher rounds off high frequencies at high levels for a smoother, darker clip; lower is brighter.
Drive.Low Cut: Input high-pass filter (Hz) before the gain; raise it to tighten the low end or remove flub, lower for fuller bass into the clipping.
Drive.High Cut: Output low-pass filter (Hz) after the gain; lower it for a darker, smoother sound, raise it for more top end and fizz.
Drive.Clip Type: Clipping circuit model (e.g. silicon, germanium, LED, tube, op-amp); changes the character and hardness of the distortion.
Drive.Bias: Bias point of the clipper, changing the balance of even and odd harmonics; extreme values sputter and can make the block go silent.
Drive.Bass: Extra low-end EQ on the drive (Fractal: up to about +/-12 dB); raise for more bass, lower for a tighter low end.
Drive.Mid: Mid boost or cut at Mid Frequency (Fractal: about +/-12 dB); raise for more midrange push, lower for a scooped sound.
Drive.Mid Frequency: Centre frequency (Hz) of the Mid control; lower it for low-mid body, raise it toward 1-2 kHz for honk and cut.
Drive.Treble: Extra high-end EQ on the drive (Fractal: about +/-12 dB); raise for brighter, lower for darker.
Drive.Bit Reduce: Lo-fi digital distortion: bits subtracted from 24-bit audio (20 gives 4-bit); leave at 0 for normal tone, raise for a gritty, broken sound.
Drive.Input Select: Which input channels feed the block: L+R sums both (default), LEFT or RIGHT uses only one side.
Drive.Balance: Pans the block's stereo output: moving left or right makes the opposite channel quieter (wet and dry); leave at 0 for centred.
Drive.Sample Rate: Lo-fi sample-rate reduction (Hz) that adds deliberate aliasing; leave at maximum 48000 for normal tone, lower for metallic, glitchy effects.
Drive.Clip Shape: With Clip Type VARIABLE, sets a custom clip curve: low values give a smooth, focused tone, high values a harder, brasher sound.
Drive.Graphic EQ: Enables the block's 10-band graphic EQ: PRE places it before the distortion, POST after it, OFF disables it.
Drive.EQ 100 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 100 Hz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for low-end weight, cut to tighten.
Drive.EQ 160 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 160 Hz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for warmth, cut to reduce boom.
Drive.EQ 250 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 250 Hz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for body, cut to reduce muddiness.
Drive.EQ 400 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 400 Hz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for thickness, cut to reduce boxiness.
Drive.EQ 640 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 640 Hz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for midrange push, cut for a scoop.
Drive.EQ 1000 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 1 kHz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost to help the tone cut through, cut to scoop or reduce honk.
Drive.EQ 1600 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 1.6 kHz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for bite and presence, cut to soften.
Drive.EQ 2500 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 2.5 kHz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for attack and edge, cut to reduce harshness.
Drive.EQ 4000 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 4 kHz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for brightness, cut to reduce fizz.
Drive.EQ 6400 Hz: Graphic EQ band at 6.4 kHz (dB, active when Graphic EQ is PRE or POST); boost for sparkle and air, cut to darken fizz.
Drive.Diode+ Type: Diode-clipping types: the diode model clipping the positive half of the wave (e.g. 1N34A germanium, LED); changes clipping hardness and character.
Drive.Diode+ Quantity: Diode-clipping types: number of diodes (1-4) clipping the positive half of the wave; experiment with type and count for new sounds.
Drive.Diode- Type: Diode-clipping types: the diode model clipping the negative half of the wave; a different type from Diode+ gives asymmetric clipping.
Drive.Diode- Quantity: Diode-clipping types: number of diodes (1-4) clipping the negative half of the wave; experiment with type and count for new sounds.
Drive.Dry Level: Clean signal passed through the diodes alongside the distortion, before the tone controls (TS types default 100%, others 0%); raise for more clarity.
Drive.Bass Response: Low-end control for Rat, Tube Screamer and similar types (their bass/voice control); raise for fuller bass, lower to tighten.
Drive.High Mid: Upper-midrange EQ on the drive (Fractal: about +/-12 dB); raise for more bite and cut, lower to soften.
Drive.Scene Ignore: Per channel: ON stops scene changes from setting this block's bypass or channel once that channel is selected; leave OFF for normal scene control.
Drive.Wicker: Big Muff types: ON engages the wicker mod, removing the circuit's feedback capacitors; OFF is the stock circuit.
Drive.Tone 2: Big Muff types: the Tone switch, which when ON bypasses the pedal's tone circuitry; OFF keeps the stock tone control in circuit.
Drive.Drive 2: Undocumented: a second gain/drive control used only by drive types that have two gain stages or knobs.
Drive.Oversampling: Runs the pedal at a higher internal rate to cut aliasing for a smoother distortion; a large CPU cost, so leave off without headroom.

Cab.Bank: Bank the first cab slot's IR comes from in Legacy mode: FACTORY 1/2 built-in IRs, USER loaded IRs, LEGACY Axe-Fx II cabs, or SCRATCHPAD.
Cab.Cab Type: Legacy mode: the IR number within the first slot's Bank, i.e. which speaker cab and mic recording is used; the biggest tone choice in the block.
Cab.Low Cut: High-pass filter (Hz) on the first IR only; raise (Fractal suggests ~80-150 Hz) to remove boomy bass, lower for fuller lows.
Cab.High Cut: Low-pass filter (Hz) on the first IR only; lower (Fractal suggests ~5-10 kHz) to tame harsh highs and darken, raise for more top end.
Cab.Bank 2: Bank the second cab slot's IR comes from in Legacy mode: FACTORY 1/2, USER, LEGACY or SCRATCHPAD.
Cab.Type: Legacy mode: the IR number within Bank 2 for the second cab slot, blended with the first IR in the cab mixer.
Cab.Level: Relative level (dB) of the first IR in the blend; with one IR it has no effect, with two it changes the mix but not overall volume.
Cab.Level 2: Relative level (dB) of the second IR in the blend; lower it to make that IR quieter in the mix, overall level stays normalised.
Cab.Pan: Stereo position of the first IR; left/right placement only, 0 for centre.
Cab.Pan 2: Stereo position of the second IR; pan the two IRs apart for a wider stereo cab sound.
Cab.Distance 1: Align delay (ms) added to the first IR, simulating a mic further back; with two IRs small delays (~0.06 ms) comb-filter and tame highs.
Cab.Distance 2: Align delay (ms) added to the second IR; offsetting one IR against the other creates mic-phase comb filtering, no effect with one IR.
Cab.Proximity: Legacy IRs: mic proximity effect on the first IR; raise for more bass (near-field), lower for a far-field colour.
Cab.Proximity 2: Legacy IRs: mic proximity effect on the second IR; raise for more bass, lower for a thinner far-field colour.
Cab.Mute1: Mixer switch for the first IR: MUTE turns it off (saves CPU), SOLO plays only it, -- leaves it active; overall level is unchanged.
Cab.Mute2: Mixer switch for the second IR: MUTE turns it off (saves CPU), SOLO plays only it, -- leaves it active.
Cab.Level 3: Master output level (dB) of the Cab block (Mix page); use this, not the IR levels, to change the block's overall volume.
Cab.Balance: Pans the block's stereo output: moving left or right makes the opposite channel quieter (wet and dry); leave at 0 for centred.
Cab.Bypass Mode: What happens when the block is bypassed: THRU passes the signal untouched like a shunt, MUTE silences it.
Cab.Mode: LEGACY picks IRs by bank and number; DYNA-CAB picks a captured cab and mic and lets you move mic position and distance.
Cab.Drive: Gain into the virtual mic preamp (needs a Preamp Type); raise toward 0 dB on its meter for warmth, compression and grit, keep low for clean.
Cab.Saturation: Ratio of even to odd harmonics in the mic preamp's distortion; only audible when Preamp Type is set and Drive is up.
Cab.Room Level: Level (%) of the built-in stereo room reverb; raise from 0 for amp-in-the-room ambience, keep low or 0 for a dry close-mic sound.
Cab.Room Size: Virtual size of the room simulator; larger gives a bigger, roomier space.
Cab.Mic Spacing: Distance between the room simulator's stereo pair of mics; raise for a wider room sound, lower for narrower.
Cab.Low Cut 2: Master high-pass filter (Hz) at the block output (Preamp page, works even with preamp off); raise to ~80-150 Hz to remove boomy bass.
Cab.High Cut 2: Master low-pass filter (Hz) at the block output (Preamp page); lower toward ~5-10 kHz to tame harsh, fizzy highs, raise for more top.
Cab.Zoom: Time zoom of the Align page graph (about 3 to 12 ms); a display setting only, it does not change the sound.
Cab.Proximity Frequency: Tunes the frequency range (Hz) over which the proximity bass boost acts; the amount is set per IR by Proximity.
Cab.Input Mode: STEREO processes left and right independently; LEFT, RIGHT or SUM L+R run the block in mono from that input.
Cab.Preamp Type: Mic preamp model (tube, FET, transformer, tape, etc.) with its own distortion character; NONE bypasses the preamp and saves CPU.
Cab.Bass: Mic preamp low-frequency tone control (dB), applied after the preamp; raise for more bass, cut to tighten.
Cab.Mid: Mic preamp midrange tone control (dB), applied after the preamp; raise for more body and push, cut to scoop.
Cab.Treble: Mic preamp high-frequency tone control (dB), applied after the preamp; raise for brighter, cut for darker.
Cab.Preamp Mode: HIGH QUALITY oversamples the mic preamp to avoid aliasing (more CPU, ~0.65 ms latency); ECONOMY uses less CPU.
Cab.Floor Reflections: Level of reflections off the virtual room floor; adjust for more or less amp-in-the-room colour.
Cab.Air: Mixes some low-pass-filtered direct (un-cabbed) signal with the cab output; a little adds air and removes boxiness, too much causes phasing.
Cab.Frequency: Air Frequency (Hz): cutoff of the direct signal mixed in by Air; set above ~3 kHz before it is noticeable, maximum gives a straight mix.
Cab.Room Shape: Type of virtual space for the room simulator: ROOM or HALL, each with its own sonic character.
Cab.LF Damping: Damps low frequencies in the virtual room; raise to make the room reverb less boomy.
Cab.HF Damping: Damps high frequencies in the virtual room; raise for a darker, softer room sound.
Cab.Room Diffusion: Diffuses discrete echoes in the virtual room; raise for a smoother room sound, lower for more distinct reflections.
Cab.Low Cut 3: High-pass filter (Hz) on the second IR only; raise to remove boomy bass from that IR.
Cab.High Cut 3: Low-pass filter (Hz) on the second IR only; lower to darken or de-harshen that IR.
Cab.IR Length: Length of the first IR: shorter STANDARD saves CPU and trims reflections but can lose low resonance and detail; ULTRA-RES keeps it all.
Cab.IR Length 2: Length of the second IR: STANDARD saves CPU and trims reflections, ULTRA-RES keeps full detail and low-end resonance.
Cab.Low Slope: Steepness of the first IR's low cut, from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct.
Cab.Low Slope 2: Steepness of the second IR's low cut, from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct.
Cab.High Slope: Steepness of the first IR's high cut, from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct.
Cab.High Slope 2: Steepness of the second IR's high cut, from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct.
Cab.Low Cut Slope: Steepness of the block's master low cut (Low Cut 2), from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct (Fractal often uses 12).
Cab.High Cut Slope: Steepness of the block's master high cut (High Cut 2), from gentle 6 dB/oct to steep 24 dB/oct (Fractal often uses 12).
Cab.Scene Ignore: Per channel: ON stops scene changes from setting this block's bypass or channel once that channel is selected; leave OFF for normal scene control.
Cab.Dynacab Type1: DynaCab mode: the captured speaker cab for the first slot (e.g. 4x12 or 1x12 models); the main cab-voicing choice in DynaCab mode.
Cab.Dynacab Type2: DynaCab mode: the captured speaker cab for the second slot, blended with the first; any cab and mic combination can be mixed.
Cab.Dynacab Mic1: DynaCab mode: microphone on the first cab; Fractal's dynamic is an SM57 (bright, harsh alone but useful in blends).
Cab.Dynacab Mic2: DynaCab mode: microphone on the second cab; Fractal notes the SM57 dynamic's extra brightness is useful when blending mics.
Cab.Dyna Cab: DynaCab mode: first mic's radial position from the speaker centre (cap) toward the edge; cap is brighter and aggressive, edge darker and warmer.
Cab.Dyna Cab 2: DynaCab mode: second mic's radial position from cap toward edge; toward the cap is brighter, toward the edge darker and warmer.
Cab.Distance: DynaCab mode: first mic's distance from the grille (0 = touching); close gives focused sound with big bass, further back less bass, more room.
Cab.Distance 3: DynaCab mode: second mic's distance from the grille; close is focused with more bass, further back gives less bass and more room.
Cab.Auto Align: ON keeps DynaCab IRs time-aligned whatever the mic Distance; OFF adds the real delay for that distance, creating phase effects between mics.

Parametric EQ.Frequency 1: Centre or cutoff frequency (Hz) of band 1, the low band; set it to where you want to shape the bass or cut low rumble.
Parametric EQ.Frequency 2: Centre frequency (Hz) of band 2; sweep it to find a low-mid area to boost or cut.
Parametric EQ.Frequency 3: Centre frequency (Hz) of band 3, the middle band; sweep to find midrange honk to cut or presence to boost.
Parametric EQ.Frequency 4: Centre frequency (Hz) of band 4; sweep to find an upper-mid area to boost for bite or cut for harshness.
Parametric EQ.Frequency 5: Centre or cutoff frequency (Hz) of band 5, the high band; set it where you want to shape treble or cut fizz.
Parametric EQ.Q 1: Bandwidth of band 1: low Q for a broad gentle change, high Q for a narrow sharp one; with Shelving 2 try 0.5-0.707 for classic overshoot.
Parametric EQ.Q 2: Bandwidth of band 2: low Q for a broad, gentle boost or cut, high Q for a narrow, surgical one.
Parametric EQ.Q 3: Bandwidth of band 3: low Q for a broad, gentle boost or cut, high Q for a narrow, surgical one.
Parametric EQ.Q 4: Bandwidth of band 4: low Q for a broad, gentle boost or cut, high Q for a narrow, surgical one.
Parametric EQ.Q 5: Bandwidth of band 5: low Q for a broad gentle change, high Q for a narrow sharp one; with Shelving 2 try 0.5-0.707 for classic overshoot.
Parametric EQ.Gain 1: Boost or cut (dB, +/-20) of band 1; positive adds, negative removes (when Type 1 is Blocking, Slope 1 sets the strength instead).
Parametric EQ.Gain 2: Boost or cut (dB, +/-20) of band 2 around Frequency 2; positive adds, negative removes.
Parametric EQ.Gain 3: Boost or cut (dB, +/-20) of band 3 around Frequency 3; positive adds, negative removes.
Parametric EQ.Gain 4: Boost or cut (dB, +/-20) of band 4 around Frequency 4; positive adds, negative removes.
Parametric EQ.Gain 5: Boost or cut (dB, +/-20) of band 5; positive adds, negative removes (when Type 5 is Blocking, Slope 5 sets the strength instead).
Parametric EQ.Type 1: Shape of band 1: Shelving lifts/cuts everything below, Peaking acts around the frequency, Blocking is a high-pass, Shelving 2 is passive-style.
Parametric EQ.Type 2: Shape of band 2: Peaking boosts or cuts around the frequency, Shelving acts beyond it; Shelving 2 is passive-style, Peaking 2 differs at low Q.
Parametric EQ.Type 3: Shape of band 3: Peaking boosts or cuts around the frequency; Peaking 2 responds differently at low Q settings.
Parametric EQ.Type 4: Shape of band 4: Peaking boosts or cuts around the frequency, Shelving acts beyond it; Shelving 2 is passive-style, Peaking 2 differs at low Q.
Parametric EQ.Type 5: Shape of band 5: Shelving lifts/cuts everything above, Peaking acts around the frequency, Blocking is a low-pass, Shelving 2 is passive-style.
Parametric EQ.Level: Overall output level (dB) of the EQ block; use it to compensate volume after boosts or cuts.
Parametric EQ.Balance: Pans the block's stereo output: moving left or right makes the opposite channel quieter (wet and dry); leave at 0 for centred.
Parametric EQ.Bypass Mode: What happens when the block is bypassed: THRU passes the signal untouched like a shunt, MUTE silences it.
Parametric EQ.S1: Solo for band 1: ON isolates that band so you can hear its role while dialling; leave OFF in a finished preset.
Parametric EQ.S2: Solo for band 2: ON isolates that band so you can hear its role while dialling; leave OFF in a finished preset.
Parametric EQ.S3: Solo for band 3: ON isolates that band so you can hear its role while dialling; leave OFF in a finished preset.
Parametric EQ.S4: Solo for band 4: ON isolates that band so you can hear its role while dialling; leave OFF in a finished preset.
Parametric EQ.S5: Solo for band 5: ON isolates that band so you can hear its role while dialling; leave OFF in a finished preset.
Parametric EQ.Slope 1: Steepness of band 1 when Type 1 is Blocking (low cut), from 6 to 36 dB/oct; steeper removes lows more decisively.
Parametric EQ.Slope 5: Steepness of band 5 when Type 5 is Blocking (high cut), from 6 to 36 dB/oct; steeper removes highs more decisively.
Parametric EQ.Scene Ignore: Per channel: ON stops scene changes from setting this block's bypass or channel once that channel is selected; leave OFF for normal scene control.
